inline:named:camera_lens/content/2/conte.annotation: Focal length used by the custom mapping (SDF custom_function/f).
inline:named:camera_lens/content/2/conte.name: f

inline:named:camera_lens/content/2/conte.annotation: Elementary mapping function applied to the scaled angle: "sin", "tan", or "id" (identity). SDF custom_function/fun.
inline:named:camera_lens/content/2/conte.name: fun

inline:named:lidar_params/content/8/cont.annotation: Minimum detectable distance (closest valid return); returns nearer than this are discarded. Unit: "m". Maps to SDF lidar/range/min.
inline:named:lidar_params/content/8/cont.name: min

inline:named:lidar_params/content/8/cont.annotation: Maximum detectable distance (farthest valid return). Unit: "m". Maps to SDF lidar/range/max.
inline:named:lidar_params/content/8/cont.name: max

inline:named:lidar_params/content/8/cont.annotation: Radial distance resolution: smallest resolvable change in measured distance along a beam. Unit: "m". Maps to SDF lidar/range/resolution. Distinct from the per-axis angular resolution in scan-pattern.
inline:named:lidar_params/content/8/cont.name: resolution

inline:root:hcdf/content/0.annotation: Human-readable description of what this HCDF file describes. For a top-level robot: the robot's purpose and key characteristics (e.g., "CogniPilot humanoid mobile base research platform with dual 7-DOF arms and TSN backbone"). For a reusable sub-assembly: the module's function and interface (e.g., "7-DOF manipulator arm with HEBI X8-series SEA actuators, 802.3dm daisy-chain, and force/torque sensing at wrist"). Helps humans and AI agents understand the file's contents without parsing the full document.
inline:root:hcdf/content/0.name: description

inline:root:hcdf/content/1.annotation: Author or organization that created this HCDF file (e.g., "CogniPilot Foundation", "HEBI Robotics", "Jane Doe"). For composed systems, each included file retains its own author, allowing BOM tools to trace which vendor or team provided each sub-assembly. Optional.
inline:root:hcdf/content/1.name: author

inline:root:hcdf/content/2.annotation: License governing use of this HCDF file and the design it describes. Use SPDX license identifiers when possible (e.g., "Apache-2.0", "BSD-3-Clause", "MIT", "CERN-OHL-S-2.0" for open hardware, "LicenseRef-Proprietary" for closed designs). For composed systems, each included file can carry a different license, enabling mixed open-source and proprietary sub-assemblies. Optional.
inline:root:hcdf/content/2.name: license

inline:root:hcdf/content/24.annotation: Reusable document-level color definitions (each @name + @rgba), referenced by name from visual <color> elements. HCDF's flat-appearance palette; replaces the former bundled <material> -- rich appearance is baked into the GLB <model>, and contact physics lives on <collision><surface>.
inline:root:hcdf/content/24.name: color

inline:root:hcdf/content/25.annotation: External HCDF file includes for model composition.
inline:root:hcdf/content/25.name: include

inline:root:hcdf/content/26.annotation: Document-level vendor/domain-specific extension data. Used (among other things) as the lax home for model-level (reference-less) URDF <gazebo> blocks and for top-level non-URDF-schema elements quarantined on import (e.g. <ros2_control> under domain "org.ros2.control"), preserving them byte-faithfully for round-trip without polluting the typed core.
inline:root:hcdf/content/26.name: extension

inline:root:hcdf/content/3.annotation: Canonical URL for this HCDF file's project, documentation, or source repository (e.g., "https://github.com/CogniPilot/hcdformat"). Provides a stable reference for humans and tooling to find updates, issues, and related resources. Optional.
inline:root:hcdf/content/3.name: url

inline:root:hcdf/content/6.annotation: Named joint groups for planning and control (e.g., left_arm, locomotion).
inline:root:hcdf/content/6.name: group

inline:root:hcdf/content/7.annotation: Named kinematic states / poses (e.g., home, transport).
inline:root:hcdf/content/7.name: state

inline:root:hcdf/content/8.annotation: Component pairs to skip for self-collision checking.
inline:root:hcdf/content/8.name: self-collision-disable

named:aerofoil_surface/content/0.annotation: Wing span (tip-to-tip for one wing, or half-span if describing one side). Unit: "m".
named:aerofoil_surface/content/0.name: span

named:aerofoil_surface/content/1.annotation: Mean aerodynamic chord (leading edge to trailing edge). Unit: "m".
named:aerofoil_surface/content/1.name: chord

named:aerofoil_surface/content/2.annotation: Airfoil profile designation (e.g., "NACA2412", "NACA0012", "ClarkY", "E387"). Determines lift/drag characteristics.
named:aerofoil_surface/content/2.name: profile

named:aerofoil_surface/content/3.annotation: Wing sweep angle. Positive = swept back. Unit: "deg".
named:aerofoil_surface/content/3.name: sweep

named:aerofoil_surface/content/4.annotation: Wing dihedral angle. Positive = tips higher than root. Affects roll stability. Unit: "deg".
named:aerofoil_surface/content/4.name: dihedral

named:aerofoil_surface/content/5.annotation: Wing planform area. Unit: "m2". If omitted, computed from span x chord.
named:aerofoil_surface/content/5.name: area

named:audio_sensor/content/0.annotation: Operating frequency range. Unit: "Hz" or "kHz". Example: min="20" max="20000" unit="Hz" for audible microphone, min="38" max="42" unit="kHz" for 40kHz ultrasonic. Defines the acoustic bandwidth.
named:audio_sensor/content/0.name: frequency-range

named:audio_sensor/content/1.annotation: Microphone sensitivity. Unit: "dBV/Pa" (typical: -44 to -26 dBV/Pa for MEMS microphones). For ultrasonic: transmit SPL in dB at reference distance.
named:audio_sensor/content/1.name: sensitivity

named:audio_sensor/content/2.annotation: Number of acoustic channels. 1 for mono, 2+ for microphone array (used for beamforming and sound localization).
named:audio_sensor/content/2.name: channels

named:audio_sensor/content/3.annotation: Acoustic beam width for directional transducers (ultrasonic, sonar). Unit: "deg". Narrower beam = longer range, lower angular coverage.
named:audio_sensor/content/3.name: beam-width

named:axis_noise/content/0.annotation: Noise model for the X channel.
named:axis_noise/content/0.name: x

named:axis_noise/content/1.annotation: Noise model for the Y channel.
named:axis_noise/content/1.name: y

named:axis_noise/content/2.annotation: Noise model for the Z channel.
named:axis_noise/content/2.name: z

named:battery_source/content/0.annotation: Cell chemistry: "LiFePO4" (3.2V/cell, safest, longest life), "Li-ion" (3.7V/cell, highest energy density), "LiPo" (3.7V/cell, high discharge rate), "NiMH" (1.2V/cell), "lead-acid" (2.0V/cell).
named:battery_source/content/0.name: chemistry

named:battery_source/content/1.annotation: Number of cells in series (determines voltage: cells x cell_voltage). Example: 8S LiFePO4 = 25.6V nominal.
named:battery_source/content/1.name: cells-series

named:battery_source/content/10.annotation: Charging protocol: "cc-cv" (constant-current then constant-voltage, standard for Li-ion/LiPo/LiFePO4), "cc" (constant-current only: NiMH, NiCd), "fast-charge" (proprietary fast-charge protocol), "trickle" (low-rate maintenance charge). Determines charger compatibility.
named:battery_source/content/10.name: charge-protocol

named:battery_source/content/11.annotation: Rated cycle life: number of charge/discharge cycles to 80% capacity retention. LiFePO4: 2000-5000 cycles. Li-ion: 300-500. LiPo: 200-300. An agent can estimate remaining battery health.
named:battery_source/content/11.name: cycle-life

named:battery_source/content/2.annotation: Number of cells in parallel (multiplies capacity and max current).
named:battery_source/content/2.name: cells-parallel

named:battery_source/content/3.annotation: Nominal pack voltage. Unit: "V". Equals cells-series x cell nominal voltage.
named:battery_source/content/3.name: nominal-voltage

named:battery_source/content/4.annotation: Battery capacity. Unit: "Ah" (amp-hours). Energy = capacity x nominal-voltage.
named:battery_source/content/4.name: capacity

named:battery_source/content/5.annotation: Total stored energy. Unit: "Wh" (watt-hours). Can be computed from capacity x voltage but useful to state explicitly.
named:battery_source/content/5.name: energy

named:battery_source/content/6.annotation: Maximum continuous discharge rate. Unit: "C" (multiples of capacity). Example: 3C on a 12Ah pack = 36A max continuous.
named:battery_source/content/6.name: max-discharge

named:battery_source/content/7.annotation: Minimum safe pack voltage (low-voltage cutoff). Unit: "V". Discharging below this damages the cells.
named:battery_source/content/7.name: min-voltage

named:battery_source/content/9.annotation: Maximum charge rate. Unit: "C" (multiples of capacity). Example: 1C on 12Ah = 12A max charge current. Fast-charge capable batteries may support 2-4C. Determines minimum charge time: time_hours = 1/charge_rate_C.
named:battery_source/content/9.name: max-charge-rate

named:box/content/0.annotation: Box dimensions as three space-separated doubles "width depth height" in meters (X Y Z extents).
named:box/content/0.name: size

named:camera_calibration/content/0.annotation: Calibrated focal length in pixels along X axis. Overrides intrinsics/fx for runtime use.
named:camera_calibration/content/0.name: fx

named:camera_calibration/content/1.annotation: Calibrated focal length in pixels along Y axis. Overrides intrinsics/fy.
named:camera_calibration/content/1.name: fy

named:camera_calibration/content/10.annotation: Date the calibration was performed in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). An agent can flag stale calibrations (e.g., older than 6 months or after a lens change).
named:camera_calibration/content/10.name: date

named:camera_calibration/content/11.annotation: Ambient temperature during calibration. Unit: "degC". Focal length varies with temperature due to thermal expansion of the lens and mount: calibrations at 20°C may not be accurate at -10°C or 50°C.
named:camera_calibration/content/11.name: temperature

named:camera_calibration/content/12.annotation: Calibration method and target used. Examples: "checkerboard-8x6-30mm" (8x6 inner corners, 30mm square size), "charuco-5x7-40mm" (ChArUco board), "apriltag-6x6-50mm", "circle-grid-4x11-asymmetric". Records how the calibration was done for reproducibility.
named:camera_calibration/content/12.name: method

named:camera_calibration/content/13.annotation: Number of calibration images used. More images generally means better coverage of the image plane and more reliable results. Typical: 20-50 images from diverse angles.
named:camera_calibration/content/13.name: images

named:camera_calibration/content/2.annotation: Calibrated principal point X in pixels. Often differs from image center by several pixels due to lens/sensor alignment.
named:camera_calibration/content/2.name: cx

named:camera_calibration/content/3.annotation: Calibrated principal point Y in pixels.
named:camera_calibration/content/3.name: cy

named:camera_calibration/content/6.annotation: Calibrated radial distortion coefficient k3 (for wide-angle lenses).
named:camera_calibration/content/6.name: k3

named:camera_calibration/content/9.annotation: RMS reprojection error from the calibration: the quality metric. Unit: "px" (pixels). Values below 0.5 px are excellent; 0.5-1.0 px is good; above 1.0 px suggests the calibration should be redone. An agent can use this to assess confidence in the calibration.
named:camera_calibration/content/9.name: reprojection-error

named:camera_distortion/content/0.annotation: First radial distortion coefficient. Positive = barrel distortion, negative = pincushion.
named:camera_distortion/content/0.name: k1

named:camera_distortion/content/2.annotation: Third radial distortion coefficient (for wide-angle lenses).
named:camera_distortion/content/2.name: k3

named:camera_distortion/content/5.annotation: Fourth distortion coefficient. Used by the rational_polynomial (8-coefficient) model and as the third fisheye term in the equidistant model. Maps to ROS CameraInfo D[5] (rational) / fisheye D[3]. Only meaningful when @model is rational_polynomial or equidistant.
named:camera_distortion/content/5.name: k4

named:camera_distortion/content/6.annotation: Fifth distortion coefficient (rational_polynomial model). Maps to ROS CameraInfo D[6].
named:camera_distortion/content/6.name: k5

named:camera_distortion/content/7.annotation: Sixth distortion coefficient (rational_polynomial model). Maps to ROS CameraInfo D[7].
named:camera_distortion/content/7.name: k6

named:camera_intrinsics/content/3.annotation: Focal length in pixels along the X axis (horizontal).
named:camera_intrinsics/content/3.name: fx

named:camera_intrinsics/content/4.annotation: Focal length in pixels along the Y axis (vertical).
named:camera_intrinsics/content/4.name: fy

named:camera_intrinsics/content/5.annotation: Principal point X coordinate in pixels (typically image_width / 2).
named:camera_intrinsics/content/5.name: cx

named:camera_intrinsics/content/6.annotation: Principal point Y coordinate in pixels (typically image_height / 2).
named:camera_intrinsics/content/6.name: cy

named:camera_intrinsics/content/7.annotation: Skew coefficient (axis skew) of the pinhole intrinsic matrix K = [[fx, s, cx], [0, fy, cy], [0, 0, 1]]. Zero for sensors with orthogonal pixel axes (virtually all modern digital sensors); non-zero only when the pixel-grid axes are non-perpendicular. Completes the 3x3 K matrix. Maps to SDF camera/lens/intrinsics/s.
named:camera_intrinsics/content/7.name: s

named:camera_lens/content/0.annotation: Half-angle from the optical axis beyond which rays are not imaged (the fisheye field limit); pixels past this angle are undefined/masked. Unit: "rad" (SI default) or "deg". Example: 1.5708 (90deg) for a 180deg circular fisheye. Maps to SDF lens/cutoff_angle.
named:camera_lens/content/0.name: cutoff-angle

named:camera_lens/content/1.annotation: If true, the projection is scaled so the configured horizontal field of view maps to the image width (SDF lens/scale_to_hfov). If false, the raw projection function determines the mapping. Default: true.
named:camera_lens/content/1.name: scale-to-hfov

named:camera_lens/content/2.annotation: Coefficients of a custom radial mapping, used when type="custom". Follows SDF lens/custom_function: image radius r = c1*f*fun(theta/c2 + c3), where theta is the angle from the optical axis and fun is the elementary function named below. Ignored for the built-in projection types.
named:camera_lens/content/2.name: custom-function

named:camera_matrix/content/0.annotation: Rectification matrix R (3x3, row-major) as nine space-separated doubles "r11 r12 r13 r21 r22 r23 r31 r32 r33". ROS CameraInfo/R: a rotation aligning the camera to the stereo-rectified/ideal frame. Identity for a monocular camera.
named:camera_matrix/content/0.name: rectification

named:camera_matrix/content/1.annotation: Projection/camera matrix P (3x4) in the rectified frame: the rectified focal length/principal point (fx'/fy'/cx'/cy') plus the baseline translation terms (tx/ty). ROS CameraInfo/P. For the right camera of a stereo pair tx encodes the baseline.
named:camera_matrix/content/1.name: projection

named:camera_matrix/content/2.annotation: Pixel binning applied by the driver (x, y). ROS CameraInfo/binning_x, binning_y. 1 (or absent) = no binning.
named:camera_matrix/content/2.name: binning

named:camera_matrix/content/3.annotation: Region of interest: the sub-window of the full sensor actually captured. ROS CameraInfo/roi. Absent => full frame.
named:camera_matrix/content/3.name: roi

named:camera_params/content/0.annotation: Shutter type: "global" (all pixels exposed simultaneously, no motion blur, required for high-speed robotics) or "rolling" (rows exposed sequentially, causes skew/wobble on fast motion, acceptable for slow scenes).
named:camera_params/content/0.name: shutter

named:camera_params/content/1.annotation: High Dynamic Range capability. true = can capture indoor shadows and outdoor sunlight in one frame. Critical for robots transitioning between lighting conditions.
named:camera_params/content/1.name: hdr

named:camera_params/content/3.annotation: For depth/RGBD cameras: usable depth measurement range. min = closest, max = farthest. Unit: "m".
named:camera_params/content/3.name: depth-range

named:camera_params/content/4.annotation: Output compression: "raw" (uncompressed, highest bandwidth: 1080p@30fps is ~1.5Gbps), "jpeg" (lossy per-frame), "h264" (lossy inter-frame), "h265" (best compression, ~5-20Mbps for 1080p). Affects network bandwidth requirements.
named:camera_params/content/4.name: compression

named:camera_params/content/5.annotation: Trigger mode: "free-running" (camera controls timing), "hardware" (external GPIO triggers capture, needed for multi-camera synchronization), "software" (software command triggers).
named:camera_params/content/5.name: trigger

named:camera_params/content/6.annotation: IR cut filter present. true = blocks infrared (standard color camera). false = passes IR (for night vision with IR illumination or NIR sensing).
named:camera_params/content/6.name: ir-cut

named:camera_params/content/7.annotation: Infrared spectral band for thermal cameras: "LWIR" (8-14um, most common, uncooled), "MWIR" (3-5um, cooled, higher sensitivity), "SWIR" (1-3um, see through fog/smoke). Not applicable for visible cameras.
named:camera_params/content/7.name: spectral-band

named:camera_params/content/8.annotation: Noise Equivalent Temperature Difference: thermal camera sensitivity. Lower = better. Unit: "mK". Typical uncooled LWIR: 40-60mK. Cooled MWIR: 15-25mK.
named:camera_params/content/8.name: netd

named:camera_params/content/9.annotation: Calibrated temperature measurement range for thermal cameras. Unit: "degC". Example: min="-20" max="150" for industrial, min="-40" max="500" for high-temp.
named:camera_params/content/9.name: temperature-range

named:camera_projection/content/0.annotation: Rectified focal length in pixels along X (P[0][0]).
named:camera_projection/content/0.name: fx

named:camera_projection/content/1.annotation: Rectified focal length in pixels along Y (P[1][1]).
named:camera_projection/content/1.name: fy

named:camera_projection/content/2.annotation: Rectified principal point X in pixels (P[0][2]).
named:camera_projection/content/2.name: cx

named:camera_projection/content/3.annotation: Rectified principal point Y in pixels (P[1][2]).
named:camera_projection/content/3.name: cy

named:camera_projection/content/4.annotation: X baseline translation term Tx (P[0][3]). Zero for the left/monocular camera; -fx'*baseline for the right camera of a horizontal stereo pair.
named:camera_projection/content/4.name: tx

named:camera_projection/content/5.annotation: Y baseline translation term Ty (P[1][3]). Nonzero only for a vertical stereo pair.
named:camera_projection/content/5.name: ty

named:capsule/content/0.annotation: Capsule radius (cylinder and hemisphere radius) in meters.
named:capsule/content/0.name: radius

named:capsule/content/1.annotation: Length of the cylindrical section in meters (excludes hemispherical caps).
named:capsule/content/1.name: length

named:collision/content/0.annotation: Pose of the collision geometry relative to the component origin (xyz/rpy or quat attributes; meters and radians). Default: identity.
named:collision/content/0.name: pose

named:collision/content/1.annotation: Geometry primitive or lean external mesh defining the collision boundary. Required. Prefer primitives/convex hulls; a collision mesh should be a lean format (STL/OBJ/convex), not a GLB -- collision needs shape, not baked appearance.
named:collision/content/1.name: geometry

named:collision/content/2.annotation: Surface physics properties (friction, restitution, contact) for this collision shape.
named:collision/content/2.name: surface

named:comp/content/0.annotation: Human-readable description of the component (e.g., "NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin compute module", "shoulder actuator assembly").
named:comp/content/0.name: description

named:comp/content/1.annotation: Board or hardware platform identifier (e.g., "jetson-agx-orin-64gb", "nxp-s32n79-evb", "custom-motor-driver-v3"). Used for BOM generation and hardware matching.
named:comp/content/1.name: board

named:comp/content/2.annotation: Operating temperature range of this component. Use min and max attributes for the rated limits. Unit: "degC" (default). Example: min="-40" max="85" for automotive grade, min="0" max="70" for commercial grade, min="-40" max="125" for mil-spec. An agent uses this to validate that all components in a system can operate in the target environment. If the robot operates outdoors in winter (-20 degC), every component's operating-temp range must include that temperature. Components without operating-temp are assumed to have no specific constraint (or the constraint is unknown).
named:comp/content/2.name: operating-temp

named:comp/content/3.annotation: Inertial properties (mass, center of mass, inertia tensor) for dynamics simulation.
named:comp/content/3.name: inertial

named:comp/content/31.annotation: Sensor group(s) on this component. Each sensor element groups related sub-sensors (IMU, camera, etc.).
named:comp/content/31.name: sensor

named:comp/content/32.annotation: Motor(s) or actuator(s) on this component. Connected to joints via transmission elements.
named:comp/content/32.name: motor

named:comp/content/33.annotation: Human-machine interface elements (displays, speakers, LEDs, buttons) on this component.
named:comp/content/33.name: hmi

named:comp/content/34.annotation: Functional interaction surfaces (aerofoils, control surfaces, propellers, wheels, tracks, grippers) on this component. Renamed from <surface> so that <surface> now refers unambiguously to collision contact physics.
named:comp/content/34.name: dynamic-surface

named:comp/content/35.annotation: Energy storage (batteries, fuel tanks) on this component.
named:comp/content/35.name: power-source

named:comp/content/36.annotation: Firmware or software identity running on this component. At most one per component.
named:comp/content/36.name: software

named:comp/content/37.annotation: Runtime discovery state (IP, port, last-seen). Populated by discovery agents, not authored by hand.
named:comp/content/37.name: discovered

named:comp/content/38.annotation: URDF-only, zero-CPS fields for this component (e.g. the PR2 link/@type). Optional; present only when imported from URDF and needed for a lossless round-trip. Omit for native HCDF.
named:comp/content/38.name: urdf-compat

named:comp/content/39.annotation: Vendor or domain-specific extension data for this component.
named:comp/content/39.name: extension

named:comp/content/4.annotation: Visual representation(s) for 3D rendering. Multiple visuals per component for multi-part models.
named:comp/content/4.name: visual

named:comp/content/5.annotation: Collision geometry for physics simulation. Multiple collision shapes per component for complex bounds.
named:comp/content/5.name: collision

named:comp/content/6.annotation: Named coordinate frames attached to this component for sensor mounts, tool points, etc.
named:comp/content/6.name: frame

named:cone/content/0.annotation: Radius of the cone base in meters.
named:cone/content/0.name: radius

named:cone/content/1.annotation: Height of the cone from base to apex in meters.
named:cone/content/1.name: length

named:control_modes/content/0.annotation: A supported control mode: "position", "velocity", "torque", "force", "current", "pwm". Multiple modes means the motor supports switching between them.
named:control_modes/content/0.name: mode

named:control_surface_def/content/0.annotation: Ratio of control surface chord to parent wing/tail chord (0-1). Typical: 0.2-0.3 for ailerons, 0.3-0.5 for flaps.
named:control_surface_def/content/0.name: chord-ratio

named:control_surface_def/content/1.annotation: Fraction of parent wing span covered by this control surface (0-1).
named:control_surface_def/content/1.name: span-fraction

named:control_surface_def/content/2.annotation: Deflection range. min = max deflection in one direction, max = other direction. Unit: "deg". Example: min="-25" max="25".
named:control_surface_def/content/2.name: deflection

named:cylinder/content/1.annotation: Cylinder length (height) along the Z axis in meters.
named:cylinder/content/1.name: length

named:data_output/content/0.annotation: Raw output data rate. Unit: "Mbps" or "Gbps". Example: 7000 Mbps for 1920x1080 RGB at 30fps uncompressed. This is the maximum bandwidth the sensor can produce.
named:data_output/content/0.name: bandwidth

named:data_output/content/1.annotation: Compressed output data rate when hardware compression is enabled. Unit: "Mbps". Example: 20 Mbps for H.265 compressed 1080p@30fps. If the sensor outputs compressed data over the network, use this for bandwidth planning instead of raw bandwidth.
named:data_output/content/1.name: bandwidth-compressed

named:data_output/content/2.annotation: Size of a single output frame/scan. Unit: "bytes". Example: 6220800 for 1920x1080x3 RGB frame. Used with update-rate to calculate bandwidth: frame-size x update-rate = bandwidth.
named:data_output/content/2.name: frame-size

named:discovered/content/0.annotation: Discovered IP address of the component (e.g., "10.0.1.42"). Populated at runtime.
named:discovered/content/0.name: ip

named:discovered/content/1.annotation: Discovered service port number (e.g., 8080 for a web interface, 7400 for DDS). Populated at runtime.
named:discovered/content/1.name: port

named:discovered/content/2.annotation: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the device was last seen online (e.g., "2026-04-05T10:30:00Z"). Populated at runtime by discovery agents.
named:discovered/content/2.name: last-seen

named:dynamic_surface/content/1.annotation: Aerodynamic lifting surface: wing, stabilizer, canard.
named:dynamic_surface/content/1.name: aerofoil

named:dynamic_surface/content/3.annotation: Aerodynamic control surface: aileron, elevator, rudder, elevon, flap.
named:dynamic_surface/content/3.name: control-surface

named:dynamic_surface/content/6.annotation: Gripper or end-effector contact surface: mechanical finger pads, suction cups, magnetic grippers, adhesive surfaces, granular jamming.
named:dynamic_surface/content/6.name: gripper

named:ellipsoid/content/0.annotation: Three semi-axis radii as "rx ry rz" in meters. Example: "0.1 0.08 0.15" for an egg-shaped ellipsoid.
named:ellipsoid/content/0.name: radii

named:flow_characterization/content/0.annotation: How fluid exits the tank: "pressurized" (self-pressurizing from stored pressure, passive, e.g., compressed gas through orifice), "regulated" (pressure regulator controls outlet pressure, active or passive mechanical, e.g., hydrogen fuel cell supply), "pumped" (electric or mechanical pump draws fluid, e.g., gasoline fuel pump), "gravity" (gravity-fed, no pressurization, e.g., open agricultural spray tanks).
named:flow_characterization/content/0.name: method

named:flow_characterization/content/1.annotation: Pressure at the tank outlet / consumer input. For regulated systems this is the regulated setpoint; for pressurized systems it decreases as the tank empties. Use min/max to capture the range. Unit: "bar" or "psi". Example: min="1.5" max="3.0" unit="bar" for a regulated hydrogen supply.
named:flow_characterization/content/1.name: outlet-pressure

named:flow_characterization/content/2.annotation: Maximum sustained (continuous) flow rate the delivery system can provide. Unit depends on fluid: "g/s" or "kg/s" for gases, "L/min" or "L/hr" for liquids, "SLPM" (standard liters per minute) for compressed gases at standard conditions. This is the continuous limit, determined by regulator capacity, pump displacement, or orifice size.
named:flow_characterization/content/2.name: max-flow-rate

named:flow_characterization/content/3.annotation: Peak (burst) flow rate available for short transients. May exceed max-flow-rate for seconds due to accumulator pressure, pump overspeed, or regulator overshoot. Unit: same as max-flow-rate. If not specified, assume peak = max (no burst capability).
named:flow_characterization/content/3.name: peak-flow-rate

named:flow_characterization/content/4.annotation: Regulation mechanism controlling outlet pressure and/or flow: "passive-mechanical" (spring-loaded diaphragm regulator: simple, no power needed), "solenoid-proportional" (electronically controlled proportional valve: precise, needs power), "solenoid-on-off" (bang-bang valve: simple digital control), "return-line" (fuel pump + return line to tank, common in automotive), "none" (unregulated: pressure drops as tank empties).
named:flow_characterization/content/4.name: regulator

named:fluid_sensor/content/0.annotation: Fluid medium being sensed (e.g. "air", "water", "seawater", "hydraulic-oil", "natural-gas"). Disambiguates otherwise-identical pressure devices: a barometer senses air, a depth sensor senses water.
named:fluid_sensor/content/0.name: medium

named:fluid_sensor/content/1.annotation: Full-scale pressure span the sensor measures, as min/max. Unit: "Pa" (SI default); "hPa"/"mbar"/"kPa"/"bar"/"psi" common. Example barometer: min="260" max="1260" unit="hPa". Example airspeed differential cell: min="0" max="6900" unit="Pa". Preferred over the inherited scalar range for pressure (which is a non-zero-based min/max span), following the tactile_sensor/pressure-range precedent.
named:fluid_sensor/content/1.name: pressure-range

named:fluid_sensor/content/10.annotation: Airspeed/pitot: smallest resolvable change in derived airspeed. Unit: "m/s".
named:fluid_sensor/content/10.name: airspeed-resolution

named:fluid_sensor/content/11.annotation: Airspeed type(s) the sensor reports: "IAS" (indicated), "CAS" (calibrated), "EAS" (equivalent), "TAS" (true). Repeatable: a density/temperature-compensated unit may output several. Free string (documented set), matching the gnss constellation/frequency convention.
named:fluid_sensor/content/11.name: airspeed-output

named:fluid_sensor/content/12.annotation: Depth sensor: derived submersion-depth output range from hydrostatic pressure. Unit: "m". Example: min="0" max="300".
named:fluid_sensor/content/12.name: depth-range

named:fluid_sensor/content/13.annotation: Level sensor: derived liquid-level (head) output range. Unit: "m". Example: min="0" max="5".
named:fluid_sensor/content/13.name: level-range

named:fluid_sensor/content/14.annotation: Flow sensor: volumetric or mass flow-rate output range. Unit: "L/min", "m3/s" (volumetric) or "kg/s" (mass). Example: min="0" max="100" unit="L/min".
named:fluid_sensor/content/14.name: flow-range

named:fluid_sensor/content/15.annotation: Flow/velocity probe geometry and ports (airspeed and flow sub-types): pitot/pitot_static/multihole/hotwire/venturi/orifice, and which static/total ports are present.
named:fluid_sensor/content/15.name: probe

named:fluid_sensor/content/2.annotation: Measurement accuracy (total error band) at reference conditions. Unit: matches the pressure unit (e.g. "hPa", "Pa") for an absolute figure, or "%FS" for percent of full scale. Example: 1.5 unit="hPa" or 0.25 unit="%FS".
named:fluid_sensor/content/2.name: accuracy

named:fluid_sensor/content/3.annotation: Compensated operating temperature range over which the accuracy spec holds. Unit: "degC". Example: min="-40" max="85".
named:fluid_sensor/content/3.name: temperature-range

named:fluid_sensor/content/4.annotation: Temperature sensitivity of the pressure reading (thermal drift). Unit: "Pa/K", "hPa/K", or "%FS/K". Lets an agent bound error when operating away from the calibration temperature.
named:fluid_sensor/content/4.name: temperature-coefficient

named:fluid_sensor/content/5.annotation: Reference/datum pressure used to derive a secondary quantity. For a barometer: the sea-level reference used for the altitude computation (ISA standard 1013.25 hPa). For a gauge/sealed transducer: the fixed reference the reading is relative to. Unit: "hPa"/"Pa".
named:fluid_sensor/content/5.name: reference-pressure

named:fluid_sensor/content/6.annotation: Reference fluid density for density-compensated derivations. For an airspeed sensor: the air density used to convert dynamic pressure to calibrated/true airspeed (ISA sea-level 1.225 kg/m3). Unit: "kg/m3".
named:fluid_sensor/content/6.name: reference-density

named:fluid_sensor/content/7.annotation: Barometer: derived pressure-altitude output range. Unit: "m". Example: min="-500" max="9000".
named:fluid_sensor/content/7.name: altitude-range

named:fluid_sensor/content/8.annotation: Barometer: smallest resolvable change in derived altitude (vertical resolution). Unit: "m". Example: 0.1 (10 cm) for a high-resolution baro.
named:fluid_sensor/content/8.name: altitude-resolution

named:fluid_sensor/content/9.annotation: Airspeed/pitot: derived airspeed output range. Unit: "m/s". Example: min="0" max="100".
named:fluid_sensor/content/9.name: airspeed-range

named:force_axis_noise/content/0.annotation: Per-axis noise on the three force channels (x/y/z). SDF force_torque/force/<x|y|z>/noise.
named:force_axis_noise/content/0.name: force

named:force_axis_noise/content/1.annotation: Per-axis noise on the three torque channels (x/y/z). SDF force_torque/torque/<x|y|z>/noise.
named:force_axis_noise/content/1.name: torque

named:force_sensor/content/0.annotation: Name of the <collision> element (on the owning component) that this contact/force sensor monitors. Maps to SDF contact/collision: required for a contact sensor to name the surface it watches. Optional here (a strain-gauge/load-cell sensor has no collision reference).
named:force_sensor/content/0.name: collision

named:force_sensor/content/1.annotation: Optional per-axis noise for a multi-axis force/torque sensor (force/x,y,z and torque/x,y,z, each a full <noise>). SDF force_torque per-axis force/torque <noise>. Complements the inherited scalar <noise> (the isotropic fallback).
named:force_sensor/content/1.name: axis-noise

named:frame/content/0.annotation: Human-readable description of the frame's purpose (e.g., "camera mount point", "tool center point").
named:frame/content/0.name: description

named:frame/content/1.annotation: Pose of the frame relative to the component origin (or to the frame named in relative-to), given via the xyz/rpy or quat attributes (meters and radians).
named:frame/content/1.name: pose

named:friction/content/0.annotation: Optional anisotropic friction (first friction direction fdir1, second-direction coefficient mu2, and per-direction slip). Present only for direction-dependent surfaces; absent => isotropic friction from @static/@dynamic.
named:friction/content/0.name: friction-direction

named:friction_direction/content/0.annotation: First friction direction as a unit vector "x y z" in the collision frame. SDF surface/friction/ode/fdir1. The second friction direction is the cross product of the contact normal and this vector. Example: "1 0 0".
named:friction_direction/content/0.name: fdir1

named:frustum/content/0.annotation: Near plane distance from sensor origin in meters.
named:frustum/content/0.name: near

named:frustum/content/1.annotation: Far plane distance from sensor origin in meters.
named:frustum/content/1.name: far

named:frustum/content/2.annotation: Full cone angle in radians (for shape="conical"). Defines a circular cross-section FOV.
named:frustum/content/2.name: fov

named:frustum/content/3.annotation: Horizontal field of view in radians (for shape="pyramidal").
named:frustum/content/3.name: hfov

named:frustum/content/4.annotation: Vertical field of view in radians (for shape="pyramidal").
named:frustum/content/4.name: vfov

named:fuel_cell/content/0.annotation: Fuel cell technology: "pem" (Proton Exchange Membrane, most common for robots, uses hydrogen), "dmfc" (Direct Methanol, uses methanol, lower power density), "sofc" (Solid Oxide, high temp, high efficiency, slow startup).
named:fuel_cell/content/0.name: type

named:fuel_cell/content/2.annotation: Continuous rated electrical power output. Unit: "W" or "kW".
named:fuel_cell/content/2.name: rated-power

named:fuel_cell/content/3.annotation: Peak (burst) electrical power output. Unit: "W" or "kW".
named:fuel_cell/content/3.name: peak-power

named:fuel_cell/content/4.annotation: Electrical conversion efficiency as a fraction (0-1). PEM typical: 0.40-0.60. SOFC typical: 0.50-0.65.
named:fuel_cell/content/4.name: efficiency

named:fuel_cell/content/5.annotation: Output voltage range. Unit: "V". Fuel cell output varies with load: min at max power, max at no load.
named:fuel_cell/content/5.name: output-voltage

named:geometry/content/1.annotation: Cylinder primitive aligned with the Z axis.
named:geometry/content/1.name: cylinder

named:geometry/content/6.annotation: External 3D mesh file reference (GLB, glTF, STL, OBJ).
named:geometry/content/6.name: mesh

named:geometry/content/7.annotation: Frustum for sensor FOV (conical or pyramidal cross-section).
named:geometry/content/7.name: frustum

named:gnss_params/content/0.annotation: Supported satellite constellation: GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou, QZSS, NavIC. More = better urban canyon performance.
named:gnss_params/content/0.name: constellation

named:gnss_params/content/1.annotation: Supported frequency band: L1, L2, L5, E1, E5a, E5b, B1, B2. Multi-frequency enables ionospheric correction.
named:gnss_params/content/1.name: frequency

named:gnss_params/content/2.annotation: RTK (Real-Time Kinematic) capable. true = cm-level positioning with base station or NTRIP corrections.
named:gnss_params/content/2.name: rtk

named:gnss_params/content/3.annotation: Horizontal accuracy without corrections (CEP50). Unit: "m". Typical: 1.5m single-freq, 1.0m multi-freq.
named:gnss_params/content/3.name: accuracy-standalone

named:gnss_params/content/4.annotation: Horizontal accuracy with RTK fix. Unit: "m". Typical: 0.01-0.02m.
named:gnss_params/content/4.name: accuracy-rtk

named:gnss_params/content/5.annotation: Pulse-Per-Second output for precise time synchronization. Can serve as time reference for gPTP or sensor timestamping.
named:gnss_params/content/5.name: pps

named:gnss_params/content/6.annotation: Built-in dead reckoning with IMU fusion for GNSS-denied environments (tunnels, urban canyons).
named:gnss_params/content/6.name: dead-reckoning

named:gnss_params/content/7.annotation: Anti-spoofing capability. Detects and rejects fake GNSS signals.
named:gnss_params/content/7.name: anti-spoofing

named:gripper_surface/content/0.annotation: Maximum grip or holding force. Unit: "N". For mechanical fingers: the squeeze force at the fingertip. For suction: the pull-off force (vacuum area x pressure differential). For magnetic: the breakaway force at contact. An agent compares this against object weight x safety factor to determine if a grasp is secure.
named:gripper_surface/content/0.name: grip-force

named:gripper_surface/content/1.annotation: Active contact area of the gripper surface. Unit: "mm2" or "cm2". For suction cups: the sealing area. For finger pads: the pad face area. For magnetic grippers: the pole face area. Larger contact area generally means more stable grasps and better force distribution.
named:gripper_surface/content/1.name: contact-area

named:gripper_surface/content/2.annotation: Maximum payload the gripper can reliably hold. Unit: "kg" or "N". This is the practical limit accounting for orientation, acceleration, and safety margin; typically less than grip-force / (gravity x safety_factor). Example: 5 kg for a two-finger gripper, 20 kg for a large vacuum gripper array.
named:gripper_surface/content/2.name: payload

named:gripper_surface/content/3.annotation: Shore durometer hardness of the contact surface material (for compliant finger pads and suction cups). Format: scale + value, e.g., "A30" (soft silicone finger pad), "A50" (medium rubber), "A70" (firm polyurethane). Shore A scale: 0=very soft gel, 30=soft rubber, 50=pencil eraser, 70=tire tread, 90=hard plastic. Softer pads conform to irregular surfaces for better grip; harder pads are more durable. Only applicable for mechanical and suction types.
named:gripper_surface/content/3.name: shore-hardness

named:gripper_surface/content/4.annotation: Vacuum pressure for suction grippers. Unit: "kPa" (negative gauge pressure). Example: -60 kPa for a standard Venturi generator, -85 kPa for a vacuum pump. Pull-off force = vacuum_level x sealing_area. Only applicable for type="suction".
named:gripper_surface/content/4.name: vacuum-level

named:gripper_surface/content/5.annotation: Magnetic holding force at contact. Unit: "N". For permanent magnets: the breakaway force with a flat mild steel surface. For electromagnets: the force at rated current. Only applicable for type="magnetic".
named:gripper_surface/content/5.name: magnetic-force

named:gripper_surface/content/6.annotation: Friction coefficients between the gripper surface and a reference material (typically smooth steel or ABS plastic). Used for grasp stability analysis: tangential holding force = normal_force x friction_coefficient.
named:gripper_surface/content/6.name: friction

named:hmi_element/content/0.annotation: Human-readable description of this HMI element.
named:hmi_element/content/0.name: description

named:hmi_element/content/1.annotation: Position and orientation relative to component origin.
named:hmi_element/content/1.name: pose

named:hmi_element/content/2.annotation: Visualization geometry for this HMI element.
named:hmi_element/content/2.name: geometry

named:hmi_element/content/3.annotation: Optical parameters of a scene-illumination HMI (a headlight, work light, or IR night-vision illuminator): the actual light source this element drives. Populated when @type="led-illumination". Maps bidirectionally to an SDF <light> (type/diffuse/specular/attenuation/direction/cast-shadows/intensity); the light's placement is the HMI <pose>. Absent => the HMI is a passive indicator with no emitted-light model.
named:hmi_element/content/3.name: illumination

named:inertial_properties/content/0.annotation: Total mass of the component in kilograms (kg).
named:inertial_properties/content/0.name: mass

named:inertial_properties/content/1.annotation: Origin of the inertial frame (center-of-mass position plus optional orientation) as a structured pose relative to the component origin. The inertia tensor below is expressed IN this frame, so a rotated inertial frame (URDF inertial/origin/@rpy) is preserved with no tensor pre-rotation. Replaces the former bare-string <com> (position only) in the clean 1.0 reset; the center of mass is inertia_origin/@xyz.
named:inertial_properties/content/1.name: inertia_origin

named:inertial_properties/content/2.annotation: Rotational inertia tensor as "ixx ixy ixz iyy iyz izz" in kg*m^2. Six unique components of the symmetric 3x3 inertia matrix about the center of mass.
named:inertial_properties/content/2.name: inertia

named:inertial_sensor/content/0.annotation: Pose of the inertial sensor relative to the sensor group origin (xyz/rpy or quat attributes; meters and radians).
named:inertial_sensor/content/0.name: pose

named:inertial_sensor/content/1.annotation: Driver identification and axis alignment for the inertial sensor IC.
named:inertial_sensor/content/1.name: driver

named:inertial_sensor/content/2.annotation: Accelerometer measurement parameters (range in g, resolution, noise, bandwidth). Present when type is "accel" or "accel_gyro".
named:inertial_sensor/content/2.name: accel

named:inertial_sensor/content/3.annotation: Gyroscope measurement parameters (range in deg/s, resolution, noise, bandwidth). Present when type is "gyro" or "accel_gyro".
named:inertial_sensor/content/3.name: gyro

named:inertial_sensor/content/4.annotation: Geometry for visualizing the inertial sensor package.
named:inertial_sensor/content/4.name: geometry

named:joint/content/0.annotation: Human-readable description of the joint's purpose (e.g., "left shoulder pitch", "front-left wheel spin").
named:joint/content/0.name: description

named:joint/content/1.annotation: Parent component of the joint. Required. The parent remains fixed while the child moves.
named:joint/content/1.name: parent

named:joint/content/10.annotation: Twist limit for a ball joint's twist DOF (rotation about the twist axis, local X): lower/upper in radians. Only valid on type="ball"; optional (omitted => unbounded twist). Paired with <swing_limit> for the two swing DOFs. Reuses joint_limit (lower/upper radians; effort Nm; velocity rad/s). Has no URDF/SDF home on export, recorded as a loss.
named:joint/content/10.name: twist_limit

named:joint/content/11.annotation: Damping, friction, and spring parameters for simulation.
named:joint/content/11.name: dynamics

named:joint/content/12.annotation: Calibration reference data for homing the joint to an absolute position.
named:joint/content/12.name: calibration

named:joint/content/13.annotation: Mimic constraint that makes this joint track another joint's position.
named:joint/content/13.name: mimic

named:joint/content/14.annotation: Loop closure marker. Present when this joint closes a kinematic loop (parallel mechanism). The kinematic tree parser should treat this joint as a constraint, not a parent-child relationship. Used for four-bar linkages, delta robots, Stewart platforms.
named:joint/content/14.name: loop

named:joint/content/15.annotation: Vendor/domain-specific extension data for this joint. Used (among other things) as the lax home for a joint-anchored URDF <gazebo reference="joint"> block on the byte-faithful import path. At most one per joint (xs:all); collect multiple domains as separate children inside it if needed.
named:joint/content/15.name: extension

named:joint/content/16.annotation: URDF-only, zero-CPS fields for this joint (e.g. safety_controller). Optional; present only when imported from URDF and needed for a lossless round-trip. Omit for native HCDF.
named:joint/content/16.name: urdf-compat

named:joint/content/2.annotation: Child component of the joint. Required. The child moves relative to the parent.
named:joint/content/2.name: child

named:joint/content/3.annotation: Pose of the joint frame relative to the parent component's origin. Defines where the joint is located and how it is oriented on the parent body.
named:joint/content/3.name: origin

named:joint/content/4.annotation: Primary axis of rotation/translation in the joint frame. Required for revolute, continuous, prismatic, cylindrical, universal, screw, and planar joints. For planar joints it is the plane NORMAL (the two DOFs translate in the plane perpendicular to it). Forbidden for fixed, free, and ball joints. For cylindrical joints, this single axis defines both the rotation and translation direction.
named:joint/content/4.name: axis

named:joint/content/5.annotation: Secondary axis for universal joints (2-DOF). Defines the second rotation axis, which must be perpendicular to the primary axis. Only valid when type="universal"; forbidden on every other joint type.
named:joint/content/5.name: axis2

named:joint/content/6.annotation: Limits for the SECOND degree of freedom. Valid ONLY on universal, cylindrical, and planar joints; forbidden on every other type. Universal: bounds axis2 (radians; maps to SDF axis2/limit). Cylindrical: bounds the rotation DOF (radians), OPTIONAL (a cylindrical joint may leave rotation unbounded). Planar: bounds the second in-plane translation range (meters). The first-DOF limits are in <limit>.
named:joint/content/6.name: limit2

named:joint/content/7.annotation: Damping/friction/spring parameters for the SECOND degree of freedom (axis2). Maps to SDF axis2/dynamics for universal/revolute2 joints. Only valid when type="universal". Optional; the primary-axis dynamics are in <dynamics>.
named:joint/content/7.name: dynamics2

named:joint/content/8.annotation: Position, velocity, effort, acceleration, and jerk limits for the FIRST degree of freedom. Required for revolute, prismatic, and cylindrical joints. Optional for continuous (velocity/effort ONLY; lower/upper are forbidden). Forbidden for fixed, free, and ball. Per-DOF meaning: for cylindrical, lower/upper are the translation range (meters) and the rotation range lives in <limit2> (radians, optional); for screw, lower/upper bound the ROTATIONAL DOF (radians) and the coupled axial translation is derived via thread_pitch; for universal, this is the primary-axis limit (radians) and axis2's is in <limit2>; for planar, this is the first in-plane translation range (meters) and the second is in <limit2>.
named:joint/content/8.name: limit

named:joint/content/9.annotation: Swing-cone limit for a ball joint's two swing DOFs (half-angles in radians; circular or elliptic cone). Only valid on type="ball"; optional (omitted => unbounded swing). Paired with <twist_limit> for the twist DOF. Has no URDF/SDF home on export (URDF spherical and classic SDF ball carry no limits), recorded as a loss.
named:joint/content/9.name: swing_limit

named:joint_group/content/0.annotation: Human-readable description of this group's purpose.
named:joint_group/content/0.name: description

named:joint_group/content/1.annotation: A joint included in this group.
named:joint_group/content/1.name: joint

named:joint_group/content/2.annotation: A sub-group included in this group (hierarchical composition).
named:joint_group/content/2.name: group

named:kinematic_state/content/0.annotation: Human-readable description of this state's purpose.
named:kinematic_state/content/0.name: description

named:kinematic_state/content/1.annotation: Position of a joint in this state. One per joint that differs from zero/default.
named:kinematic_state/content/1.name: joint-position

named:led_illumination/content/0.annotation: Diffuse light colour as four space-separated doubles "r g b a" (0-1). SDF light/diffuse.
named:led_illumination/content/0.name: diffuse

named:led_illumination/content/1.annotation: Specular light colour as four space-separated doubles "r g b a" (0-1). SDF light/specular.
named:led_illumination/content/1.name: specular

named:led_illumination/content/2.annotation: Emission direction as three space-separated doubles "x y z" (unit vector), for spot and directional lights. SDF light/direction.
named:led_illumination/content/2.name: direction

named:lidar_params/content/0.annotation: Scanning mechanism: "mechanical" (spinning head: 360° FOV but vibration-sensitive, has wear parts), "solid-state" (no moving parts, limited FOV, very robust), "mems" (MEMS mirror, compact, moderate FOV), "flash" (illuminates entire scene at once, short range, no scanning).
named:lidar_params/content/0.name: scan-type

named:lidar_params/content/1.annotation: Number of vertical channels (laser/detector pairs). More = denser vertical coverage. Typical: 16, 32, 64, 128.
named:lidar_params/content/1.name: channels

named:lidar_params/content/10.annotation: Range/beam noise model for the lidar (SDF lidar/ray <noise>). Applies to the measured distance along each beam. Optional; absent => ideal (noiseless) ranging.
named:lidar_params/content/10.name: noise

named:lidar_params/content/2.annotation: Total point measurement rate. Determines point cloud density and downstream processing/bandwidth. Example: 300000 (Livox Mid-360), 1200000 (Hesai XT32).
named:lidar_params/content/2.name: points-per-second

named:lidar_params/content/3.annotation: Frame/rotation rate. For mechanical: rotations per second. For solid-state: frame rate. Unit: "Hz". Typical: 10-20.
named:lidar_params/content/3.name: scan-rate

named:lidar_params/content/4.annotation: Return mode: "single" (first or strongest only), "dual" (first + strongest), "triple" (first + second + strongest). Multi-return sees through rain, dust, and vegetation.
named:lidar_params/content/4.name: returns

named:lidar_params/content/5.annotation: Laser wavelength. 905nm = common, lower cost, affected by sunlight. 1550nm = eye-safe at higher power, better rain/fog penetration, more expensive. Unit: "nm".
named:lidar_params/content/5.name: wavelength

named:lidar_params/content/6.annotation: Horizontal field of view. 360 for spinning lidars, 60-120 for solid-state. Unit: "deg".
named:lidar_params/content/6.name: horizontal-fov

named:lidar_params/content/7.annotation: Vertical field of view as min/max angle. Example: min="-25" max="15" unit="deg".
named:lidar_params/content/7.name: vertical-fov

named:lidar_params/content/8.annotation: Distance measurement range of the ranging sensor: minimum and maximum detectable distance and the radial (range) resolution. Maps losslessly to SDF lidar/<range> (min/max/resolution). Distinct from the angular scan-pattern (which describes sweep angles): this is the along-beam distance the sensor can report.
named:lidar_params/content/8.name: range

named:lidar_params/content/9.annotation: Per-axis angular scan pattern (samples/resolution/min-angle/max-angle for the horizontal and vertical axes), the lossless target for a converted URDF ray/LaserRay sensor. Optional; complements the aggregate channels/fov fields above.
named:lidar_params/content/9.name: scan-pattern

named:light_attenuation/content/0.annotation: Maximum range of the light in meters: beyond this the light contributes nothing. SDF light/attenuation/range.
named:light_attenuation/content/0.name: range

named:light_attenuation/content/1.annotation: Linear attenuation factor (0-1): 1 attenuates evenly over the range. SDF light/attenuation/linear.
named:light_attenuation/content/1.name: linear

named:light_attenuation/content/2.annotation: Constant attenuation factor: 1.0 never attenuates, 0.0 is complete attenuation. SDF light/attenuation/constant.
named:light_attenuation/content/2.name: constant

named:light_attenuation/content/3.annotation: Quadratic attenuation factor: adds curvature to the falloff. SDF light/attenuation/quadratic.
named:light_attenuation/content/3.name: quadratic

named:loop_closure/content/0.annotation: Predecessor body (comp name) in the kinematic loop at this closure point.
named:loop_closure/content/0.name: predecessor

named:loop_closure/content/1.annotation: Successor body (comp name) in the kinematic loop at this closure point.
named:loop_closure/content/1.name: successor

named:loop_closure/content/2.annotation: 6-value string "tx ty tz rx ry rz" where 1=constrained, 0=free. Example: "1 1 1 1 1 0" constrains all except rotation around Z.
named:loop_closure/content/2.name: constraint-axes

named:mesh/content/0.annotation: Optional selection of a single named sub-part within the mesh file (SDF mesh/submesh). Absent => load the whole file.
named:mesh/content/0.name: submesh

named:model_ref/content/0.annotation: Include-mode selector: draw this named node subtree; repeated, the UNION of several. Reuses the <submesh> type (name + optional @center). The subtree keeps its model-root-relative transform (no recenter). @center is honored only when this is the LONE selector on the <model> (one <submesh>, no siblings, no exclusions); the validator rejects @center on a union member. MUST NOT be combined with <exclude-submesh>; mixing include and exclude is a validator error.
named:model_ref/content/0.name: submesh

named:model_ref/content/1.annotation: Exclude-mode selector: draw the whole model MINUS this named node subtree; repeated, minus all of them. The complement of <submesh>; the dedicated type carries no @center (a subtraction has nothing to recenter). MUST NOT be combined with <submesh>; mixing exclude and include is a validator error. Motivating case: a shared actuator GLB whose case visual is the whole model excluding the flange subtree (case, connectors, and pin anchors come along implicitly as the CAD grows), paired with a flange visual on the sibling comp that is the matching <submesh> include.
named:model_ref/content/1.name: exclude-submesh

named:motor/content/0.annotation: Pose of the motor relative to the component origin (xyz/rpy or quat attributes; meters and radians).
named:motor/content/0.name: pose

named:motor/content/1.annotation: Motor voltage ratings with nominal/continuous/peak/max levels. Unit: typically "V".
named:motor/content/1.name: voltage

named:motor/content/10.annotation: Thermal resistance from winding to ambient. Unit: typically "degC/W". Used for thermal derating calculations.
named:motor/content/10.name: thermal-resistance

named:motor/content/11.annotation: Maximum allowable winding temperature before demagnetization or insulation failure. Unit: typically "degC".
named:motor/content/11.name: max-temperature

named:motor/content/12.annotation: Direction of thrust force as "x y z" unit vector relative to the component frame. Only for type="thrust". Example: "0 0 1" for upward thrust.
named:motor/content/12.name: thrust-axis

named:motor/content/13.annotation: Maximum thrust force output. Unit: "N". Only for type="thrust".
named:motor/content/13.name: max-thrust

named:motor/content/14.annotation: Number of magnetic pole pairs in the motor. Determines the electrical frequency: electrical_freq = mechanical_rpm × pole_pairs / 60. Critical for BLDC commutation (Hall sensor transitions per revolution = pole_pairs × 6), ESC configuration, and back-EMF frequency. Example: 15 pole pairs for ZLLG65ASM250-L hub motor, 7 for typical drone motor, 2 for industrial servo.
named:motor/content/14.name: pole-pairs

named:motor/content/15.annotation: Engine displacement for internal combustion motors. Unit: "cc" (cubic centimeters) or "L" (liters). Only applicable for type="ice". Example: 50cc for a small generator, 0.8L for a robot mower engine.
named:motor/content/15.name: displacement

named:motor/content/16.annotation: Number of cylinders for internal combustion motors. Only applicable for type="ice".
named:motor/content/16.name: cylinders

named:motor/content/17.annotation: Linear travel range for linear actuators. Unit: "m" or "mm". Defines the maximum extension distance. Only applicable for type="linear".
named:motor/content/17.name: stroke

named:motor/content/18.annotation: Supported control interfaces for this motor.
named:motor/content/18.name: control-modes

named:motor/content/19.annotation: No-load shaft speed at rated voltage. Unit: "rpm". From motor load test. Higher than rated speed. Example: 257.9 rpm for ZLLG65ASM250-L at 24V.
named:motor/content/19.name: no-load-speed

named:motor/content/2.annotation: Motor current ratings with nominal/continuous/peak/max levels. Unit: typically "A".
named:motor/content/2.name: current

named:motor/content/20.annotation: No-load current draw at rated voltage. Unit: "A". The minimum current the motor draws when spinning freely. Important for idle power budget. Example: 0.974A.
named:motor/content/20.name: no-load-current

named:motor/content/21.annotation: Maximum mechanical power output from load test. Unit: "W". The peak of the power-vs-torque curve. Example: 158.8W at 11.61 Nm for ZLLG65ASM250-L.
named:motor/content/21.name: max-power-out

named:motor/content/22.annotation: Peak efficiency from load test. Unit: "percent". The best-case power_out/power_in ratio. Example: 68.4% at 3.84 Nm / 216.3 RPM. An agent should target this operating point for best runtime.
named:motor/content/22.name: max-efficiency

named:motor/content/4.annotation: Phase (winding) inductance. Unit: typically "H" (henries) or "mH". A standard BLDC datasheet parameter alongside resistance; the L/R electrical time constant sets the current-loop bandwidth for field-oriented control.
named:motor/content/4.name: inductance

named:motor/content/5.annotation: Motor torque constant (Kt). Torque output per ampere of current. Unit: typically "Nm/A".
named:motor/content/5.name: torque-constant

named:motor/content/6.annotation: Motor velocity constant: the proportionality between voltage and rotational speed. This single element covers both Ke (back-EMF constant) and Kv (speed constant) conventions; the unit attribute determines which: use unit="V/RPM" or unit="V.s/rad" for Ke (back-EMF style, common on industrial servo and hub motor datasheets, e.g., 0.109 V/RPM for ZLLG65ASM250-L); use unit="RPM/V" for Kv (speed constant style, common on drone/RC BLDC datasheets, e.g., 920 RPM/V). Ke and Kv are reciprocals of each other; an agent computes one from the other as needed.
named:motor/content/6.name: velocity-constant

named:motor/content/7.annotation: Rotor moment of inertia (J) about the motor's rotation axis. Unit: typically "kg.m^2" or "g.cm^2". The rotor's own inertia reflected through a transmission dominates the effective inertia at the joint (reflected_inertia = rotor_inertia x reduction^2), so it is required for the reflected-inertia and acceleration math on quasi-direct-drive (QDD) actuators.
named:motor/content/7.name: rotor-inertia

named:motor/content/8.annotation: Maximum no-load shaft speed. Unit: typically "rpm" or "rad/s".
named:motor/content/8.name: max-speed

named:motor/content/9.annotation: Stall torque at rated voltage. Unit: typically "Nm".
named:motor/content/9.name: stall-torque

named:noise/content/0.annotation: Mean of the noise distribution. Default: 0. Units match the sensor's measurement unit.
named:noise/content/0.name: mean

named:noise/content/1.annotation: Standard deviation of the noise distribution. Default: 0. Units match the sensor's measurement unit.
named:noise/content/1.name: stddev

named:noise/content/2.annotation: Mean of the static bias distribution. Default: 0. Units match the sensor's measurement unit.
named:noise/content/2.name: bias-mean

named:noise/content/3.annotation: Standard deviation of the static bias distribution. Default: 0. Units match the sensor's measurement unit.
named:noise/content/3.name: bias-stddev

named:noise/content/4.annotation: Quantization precision (ADC resolution). Output is rounded to the nearest multiple of this value. Units match the sensor's measurement unit.
named:noise/content/4.name: precision

named:noise/content/5.annotation: Standard deviation of the DYNAMIC bias process: a slowly time-varying bias (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck / first-order Gauss-Markov), distinct from the static bias random walk (bias-mean/bias-stddev). Maps to SDF noise/dynamic_bias_stddev. Default: 0 (no dynamic bias). Units match the sensor's measurement unit.
named:noise/content/5.name: dynamic-bias-stddev

named:noise/content/6.annotation: Correlation time (in seconds) of the dynamic bias process: the time constant over which the dynamic bias decorrelates. Maps to SDF noise/dynamic_bias_correlation_time. Larger values = slower drift. Only meaningful when dynamic-bias-stddev is set.
named:noise/content/6.name: dynamic-bias-correlation-time

named:optical_sensor/content/0.annotation: Pose of the optical sensor module relative to the sensor group origin (xyz/rpy or quat attributes; meters and radians).
named:optical_sensor/content/0.name: pose

named:optical_sensor/content/1.annotation: Driver identification for the optical sensor (e.g., "oak-d-pro", "rplidar-a2", "vl53l5cx").
named:optical_sensor/content/1.name: driver

named:optical_sensor/content/2.annotation: Geometry for visualizing the optical sensor housing.
named:optical_sensor/content/2.name: geometry

named:optical_sensor/content/3.annotation: Field-of-view definition(s). One per sensing cone/pyramid. Stereo cameras have two FoVs; omnidirectional lidars may have one 360-degree FoV.
named:optical_sensor/content/3.name: fov

named:optical_sensor/content/4.annotation: Output bandwidth for network planning. Cameras and lidars generate significant data; an agent uses this to validate TSN schedules and link capacity.
named:optical_sensor/content/4.name: data-output

named:optical_sensor/content/5.annotation: Camera-specific parameters (shutter, HDR, compression, trigger, thermal specs). Use when type="camera" or type="thermal".
named:optical_sensor/content/5.name: camera-params

named:optical_sensor/content/6.annotation: Lidar-specific parameters (scan-type, channels, points-per-second, returns, wavelength). Use when type="lidar".
named:optical_sensor/content/6.name: lidar-params

named:power_source/content/2.annotation: Fuel cell energy converter (PEM, DMFC, SOFC). Generates electricity from fuel continuously.
named:power_source/content/2.name: fuel-cell

named:power_source/content/3.annotation: Solar panel energy source. Generates electricity from sunlight via photovoltaic cells.
named:power_source/content/3.name: solar

named:power_source/content/4.annotation: Supercapacitor for peak power buffering, regenerative braking energy capture, and pulsed load smoothing.
named:power_source/content/4.name: supercapacitor

named:prop_surface/content/1.annotation: Propeller pitch: theoretical distance advanced per revolution in ideal fluid. Unit: "m" or "in".
named:prop_surface/content/1.name: pitch

named:prop_surface/content/3.annotation: Rotation direction viewed from above/front: "CW" (clockwise) or "CCW" (counter-clockwise). Critical for torque balancing on multirotors.
named:prop_surface/content/3.name: direction

named:radar_params/content/0.annotation: Operating frequency. 77-79GHz = automotive standard (high resolution). 24GHz = industrial (longer range, lower resolution). Unit: "GHz".
named:radar_params/content/0.name: frequency

named:radar_params/content/1.annotation: Modulation scheme: "fmcw" (Frequency-Modulated Continuous Wave, automotive standard, measures range + velocity simultaneously) or "pulsed" (traditional, longer range).
named:radar_params/content/1.name: modulation

named:radar_params/content/10.annotation: MIMO antenna configuration as "NtxMrx" (e.g., "3tx4rx" = 12 virtual channels). More virtual channels = better angular resolution.
named:radar_params/content/10.name: mimo

named:radar_params/content/2.annotation: Horizontal field of view. Unit: "deg". Typical: 120 short-range, 20 long-range.
named:radar_params/content/2.name: azimuth-fov

named:radar_params/content/3.annotation: Vertical field of view (4D imaging radar). Unit: "deg". Presence indicates elevation-capable radar.
named:radar_params/content/3.name: elevation-fov

named:radar_params/content/4.annotation: Azimuth angular resolution: minimum angle to separate two targets horizontally. Unit: "deg".
named:radar_params/content/4.name: azimuth-resolution

named:radar_params/content/6.annotation: Range resolution: minimum distance to separate two targets at the same angle. Unit: "m". Determined by chirp bandwidth.
named:radar_params/content/6.name: range-resolution

named:radar_params/content/8.annotation: Velocity resolution: minimum speed difference to separate two targets. Unit: "m/s".
named:radar_params/content/8.name: velocity-resolution

named:radar_params/content/9.annotation: Maximum simultaneous target detections per frame.
named:radar_params/content/9.name: max-detections

named:rf_sensor/content/0.annotation: Radar-specific parameters (frequency, modulation, FOV, resolution, velocity, MIMO). Use when type="radar".
named:rf_sensor/content/0.name: radar-params

named:rf_sensor/content/1.annotation: GNSS-specific parameters (constellations, frequencies, RTK, accuracy, PPS). Use when type="gnss".
named:rf_sensor/content/1.name: gnss-params

named:self_collision_disable/content/0.annotation: A pair of components to disable collision checking between.
named:self_collision_disable/content/0.name: pair

named:sensor/content/0.annotation: Inertial measurement unit(s): accelerometers and/or gyroscopes.
named:sensor/content/0.name: inertial

named:sensor/content/1.annotation: Electromagnetic sensor(s): magnetometers, metal detectors, eddy current probes.
named:sensor/content/1.name: em

named:sensor/content/10.annotation: Tactile/contact sensor(s): capacitive arrays, FSR pads, piezoelectric skins, barometric patches, optical gel sensors. Provides spatially distributed pressure/contact data for grasp planning, slip detection, and safe interaction.
named:sensor/content/10.name: tactile

named:sensor/content/11.annotation: Fluid sensor(s): barometers, airspeed/pitot sensors, depth sensors, flow meters, liquid-level sensors, and general pressure transducers. Measurand is gas/liquid pressure or flow (distinct from force = solid contact and chemical = composition).
named:sensor/content/11.name: fluid

named:sensor/content/2.annotation: Optical sensor(s): cameras, lidars, ToF sensors, optical flow sensors.
named:sensor/content/2.name: optical

named:sensor/content/3.annotation: Radio-frequency sensor(s): GNSS receivers, UWB rangers, radars, radio altimeters.
named:sensor/content/3.name: rf

named:sensor/content/4.annotation: Chemical/environmental sensor(s): gas detectors, pH sensors, humidity sensors.
named:sensor/content/4.name: chemical

named:sensor/content/5.annotation: Force/torque sensor(s): strain gauges, pressure transducers, torque sensors, load cells.
named:sensor/content/5.name: force

named:sensor/content/6.annotation: Position/velocity encoder(s): motor-side, joint-side, wheel, or linear. Optical, magnetic, inductive, capacitive, or resistive principle.
named:sensor/content/6.name: encoder

named:sensor/content/7.annotation: Temperature sensor(s): thermistors, RTDs, thermocouples, IR. Common: motor winding temp, battery cell temp, ambient.
named:sensor/content/7.name: temperature

named:sensor/content/8.annotation: Radiation sensor(s): Geiger counters, scintillation detectors, neutron sensors, dosimeters.
named:sensor/content/8.name: radiation

named:sensor/content/9.annotation: Audio/acoustic sensor(s): microphones, ultrasonic transducers, sonar, hydrophones.
named:sensor/content/9.name: audio

named:sensor_base/content/0.annotation: Pose of the sensor relative to the component origin (xyz/rpy or quat attributes; meters and radians).
named:sensor_base/content/0.name: pose

named:sensor_base/content/1.annotation: Driver IC identification and axis alignment configuration.
named:sensor_base/content/1.name: driver

named:sensor_base/content/4.annotation: Noise model for the sensor output.
named:sensor_base/content/4.name: noise

named:sensor_base/content/5.annotation: Output bandwidth and frame size for network planning. Only needed for sensors that transmit significant data over the network (cameras, lidars, radars).
named:sensor_base/content/5.name: data-output

named:sensor_driver/content/0.annotation: Axis remapping from sensor internal axes to component body frame. Optional; omit if sensor axes match body frame.
named:sensor_driver/content/0.name: axis-align

named:sensor_fov/content/0.annotation: Human-readable description of this FoV (e.g., "left stereo camera", "forward-facing depth").
named:sensor_fov/content/0.name: description

named:sensor_fov/content/1.annotation: Pose of the FoV origin relative to the sensor origin (xyz/rpy or quat attributes; meters and radians). For stereo cameras, this encodes the baseline offset.
named:sensor_fov/content/1.name: pose

named:sensor_fov/content/2.annotation: FoV volume geometry for visualization. Typically a frustum (conical or pyramidal).
named:sensor_fov/content/2.name: geometry

named:sensor_fov/content/3.annotation: Design-spec camera intrinsic parameters (focal length, principal point, image size) from the datasheet. For calibrated values, use the calibration element instead.
named:sensor_fov/content/3.name: intrinsics

named:sensor_fov/content/4.annotation: Design-spec lens distortion coefficients (Brown-Conrady model). For calibrated values, use the calibration element instead.
named:sensor_fov/content/4.name: distortion

named:sensor_fov/content/5.annotation: Lens projection model (fisheye/wide-angle mapping function and field cutoff). Present for non-rectilinear lenses that Brown-Conrady distortion cannot describe; absent => pinhole/rectilinear projection per the intrinsics.
named:sensor_fov/content/5.name: lens

named:sensor_fov/content/6.annotation: Measured calibration results for this specific camera unit. Contains calibrated intrinsics (fx, fy, cx, cy), distortion coefficients (k1-k3, p1-p2), reprojection error, calibration date, temperature, and method. When present, agents should use these values instead of the design-spec intrinsics/distortion.
named:sensor_fov/content/6.name: calibration

named:sensor_fov/content/7.annotation: Per-pixel noise model for this FoV (e.g., depth noise for ToF sensors).
named:sensor_fov/content/7.name: noise

named:sensor_fov/content/8.annotation: Full ROS CameraInfo geometry for this FoV beyond the K matrix (intrinsics) and D coefficients (distortion): the rectification matrix R, projection matrix P, pixel binning, and region of interest. Present for a stereo-rectified or cropped/binned camera. Absent => identity rectification, P = K, no binning, full frame.
named:sensor_fov/content/8.name: camera-matrix

named:sensor_params/content/0.annotation: Full-scale measurement range (e.g., 16 with unit="g" for +/-16g accelerometer, 2000 with unit="dps" for gyroscope).
named:sensor_params/content/0.name: range

named:sensor_params/content/1.annotation: Measurement resolution: smallest detectable change (e.g., 0.488 with unit="mg" for 16-bit at 16g range).
named:sensor_params/content/1.name: resolution

named:sensor_params/content/2.annotation: Output Data Rate: hardware sampling frequency in Hz. This is how fast the ADC converts, regardless of how often software processes the data. Example: 3200 with unit="Hz". Determines Nyquist frequency (odr/2) and aliasing behavior.
named:sensor_params/content/2.name: odr

named:sensor_params/content/3.annotation: Anti-aliasing low-pass filter cutoff frequency in Hz. Determines the useful signal bandwidth. Typically at or below ODR/2 (Nyquist). Example: 1600 with unit="Hz" for ODR=3200Hz. Lower bandwidth reduces noise but limits frequency response.
named:sensor_params/content/3.name: bandwidth

named:sensor_params/content/4.annotation: Hardware FIFO buffer configuration. When present, the sensor collects samples at ODR rate into a buffer and interrupts at ODR/watermark rate. Example: ODR=3200Hz, fifo watermark=8 → 400Hz interrupt rate delivering 8 samples per burst.
named:sensor_params/content/4.name: fifo

named:sensor_params/content/5.annotation: Noise model for this measurement axis. Includes measurement-distribution standard deviation, static and dynamic bias terms, and quantization precision. Scalar (isotropic): applies to all three physical axes. For anisotropic per-axis noise, use axis-noise below (this scalar is the fallback).
named:sensor_params/content/5.name: noise

named:sensor_params/content/6.annotation: Optional per-axis noise (x/y/z), each a full <noise> model. Present when the accelerometer/gyroscope specifies different noise on each axis (SDF gz-sim per-axis <angular_velocity>/<linear_acceleration> <x|y|z>/<noise> blocks). Complements the scalar <noise> above, which remains the isotropic fallback.
named:sensor_params/content/6.name: axis-noise

named:software/content/0.annotation: Firmware or software version string (e.g., "1.2.3", "v2024.03-rc1"). Semantic versioning recommended.
named:software/content/0.name: version

named:software/content/1.annotation: SHA-256 hash of the firmware binary for integrity verification and update tracking.
named:software/content/1.name: hash

named:software/content/2.annotation: URI of the firmware manifest file describing the full firmware package contents, dependencies, and update instructions.
named:software/content/2.name: firmware-manifest-uri

named:software/content/3.annotation: Runtime configuration parameters string passed to the firmware at boot (e.g., DTS overlay name, boot arguments).
named:software/content/3.name: params

named:solar_source/content/0.annotation: Photovoltaic cell technology: "monocrystalline" (highest efficiency 20-24%, rigid panels), "polycrystalline" (lower cost, 15-20% efficiency), "thin-film" (flexible, lightweight, 10-15% efficiency, can conform to curved surfaces), "gaas" (gallium arsenide, 28-30% efficiency, used in space, expensive), "perovskite" (emerging, potentially low cost). Determines efficiency, weight, flexibility, and cost tradeoffs.
named:solar_source/content/0.name: cell-type

named:solar_source/content/1.annotation: Peak power output under Standard Test Conditions (STC: 1000 W/m2 irradiance, 25 degC cell temperature, AM1.5 spectrum). Unit: "W" or "Wp" (watts-peak). Real-world output is typically 60-80% of peak due to non-ideal conditions. Example: 100 Wp panel produces ~60-80W in typical outdoor conditions.
named:solar_source/content/1.name: peak-power

named:solar_source/content/2.annotation: Total panel area. Unit: "m2" or "cm2". Used with efficiency to cross-check peak-power: peak_power = area x 1000W/m2 x efficiency. Also used for physical packaging constraints on the robot body.
named:solar_source/content/2.name: area

named:solar_source/content/3.annotation: Solar cell conversion efficiency as a fraction (0-1). The ratio of electrical power output to incident solar power. Monocrystalline: 0.20-0.24. Polycrystalline: 0.15-0.20. Thin-film: 0.10-0.15. GaAs: 0.28-0.30.
named:solar_source/content/3.name: efficiency

named:solar_source/content/4.annotation: Voltage at Maximum Power Point (Vmpp) under STC. Unit: "V". The MPPT charge controller operates the panel at this voltage to extract maximum power. Example: 18V for a nominal 12V panel, 36V for a nominal 24V panel.
named:solar_source/content/4.name: voltage-mpp

named:solar_source/content/5.annotation: Current at Maximum Power Point (Impp) under STC. Unit: "A". peak-power = voltage-mpp x current-mpp.
named:solar_source/content/5.name: current-mpp

named:solar_source/content/6.annotation: Open-circuit voltage (Voc) under STC. Unit: "V". The maximum voltage the panel produces with no load. Always higher than voltage-mpp. Used for charge controller input voltage rating.
named:solar_source/content/6.name: open-circuit-voltage

named:solar_source/content/7.annotation: Whether the associated charge controller uses Maximum Power Point Tracking. true = MPPT controller (extracts 15-30% more energy than PWM in varying conditions). false = PWM or direct connection. An agent factors this into energy harvest estimates.
named:solar_source/content/7.name: mppt

named:supercapacitor_source/content/0.annotation: Total capacitance. Unit: "F" (farads). Supercapacitors typically range from 1F to 3000F per cell. Series/parallel configurations adjust the effective capacitance and voltage. Energy stored = 0.5 x C x V^2.
named:supercapacitor_source/content/0.name: capacitance

named:supercapacitor_source/content/1.annotation: Maximum rated voltage. Unit: "V". Individual cells are typically 2.5-2.7V; series stacks reach 12V, 24V, 48V or higher. Exceeding max voltage causes gas generation and permanent damage.
named:supercapacitor_source/content/1.name: max-voltage

named:supercapacitor_source/content/2.annotation: Equivalent Series Resistance. Unit: "mohm" (milliohms). Determines power loss during charge/discharge and maximum current capability: I_max approx V / ESR. Lower ESR = higher power capability. Typical: 0.3-50 mohm depending on size.
named:supercapacitor_source/content/2.name: esr

named:supercapacitor_source/content/3.annotation: Maximum continuous discharge current. Unit: "A". Supercapacitors can deliver very high currents (hundreds of amps) for short durations. Limited by ESR heating.
named:supercapacitor_source/content/3.name: max-current

named:supercapacitor_source/content/4.annotation: Peak (burst) current for short pulses. Unit: "A". Can be significantly higher than max-current for pulses under 1 second.
named:supercapacitor_source/content/4.name: peak-current
