named:supercapacitor_source/content/5.annotation: Total stored energy at max voltage. Unit: "Wh" or "J". Computed from 0.5 x C x V^2 but useful to state explicitly. Much less than batteries of similar volume: a 3000F/2.7V cell stores ~3 Wh vs ~50 Wh for a similar-sized Li-ion cell.
named:supercapacitor_source/content/5.name: energy

named:supercapacitor_source/content/6.annotation: Number of cells in series. Determines pack voltage: max-voltage = cells x cell-voltage. Requires balancing circuitry.
named:supercapacitor_source/content/6.name: cells-series

named:supercapacitor_source/content/7.annotation: Rated cycle life: number of charge/discharge cycles to 80% capacitance retention. Supercapacitors typically last 500,000 to 1,000,000+ cycles, far exceeding batteries.
named:supercapacitor_source/content/7.name: cycle-life

named:surface/content/1.annotation: Coefficient of restitution (bounciness). 0 = perfectly inelastic (no bounce), 1 = perfectly elastic (full bounce). Dimensionless, range [0, 1].
named:surface/content/1.name: restitution

named:surface/content/2.annotation: Contact dynamics parameters (stiffness, damping) for physics simulation.
named:surface/content/2.name: contact

named:tactile_sensor/content/0.annotation: Number of rows in the taxel array. Defines the spatial layout along one axis of the sensing surface. Example: 4 rows x 4 cols = 16 taxels in a fingertip pad.
named:tactile_sensor/content/0.name: rows

named:tactile_sensor/content/1.annotation: Number of columns in the taxel array. Together with rows, defines the rectangular grid of sensing elements.
named:tactile_sensor/content/1.name: cols

named:tactile_sensor/content/2.annotation: Total number of individual tactile sensing elements (taxels). For regular grids, taxels = rows x cols. For irregular layouts (e.g., curved fingertip, hexagonal packing), specify taxels directly when rows/cols do not apply. Example: 160 taxels on a SynTouch BioTac, 32 on a XELA uSkin patch.
named:tactile_sensor/content/2.name: taxels

named:tactile_sensor/content/3.annotation: Center-to-center spacing between adjacent taxels. Unit: "mm". Determines the minimum feature size the sensor can resolve through touch. Example: 2.5 mm for a fingertip array, 10 mm for a body-skin patch. Smaller spacing = finer spatial detail but more wiring and processing.
named:tactile_sensor/content/3.name: spatial-resolution

named:tactile_sensor/content/4.annotation: Measurable contact pressure range per taxel. Unit: "kPa" or "N". min = minimum detectable pressure (sensitivity threshold), max = saturation pressure. Example: min="0.1" max="100" unit="kPa" for a capacitive fingertip. Light touch is ~1 kPa, firm grip is 10-50 kPa, maximum grip can exceed 100 kPa.
named:tactile_sensor/content/4.name: pressure-range

named:tactile_sensor/content/5.annotation: Total active sensing area of the tactile surface. Unit: "mm2" or "cm2". Example: 314 mm2 for a circular fingertip pad (20mm diameter), 2500 mm2 for a 50x50 palm patch.
named:tactile_sensor/content/5.name: sensing-area

named:tank_source/content/0.annotation: Fuel type: "gasoline", "diesel", "hydrogen", "compressed-air", "nitrogen", "propane", "ethanol", "jet-a". Determines energy density and handling requirements.
named:tank_source/content/0.name: fuel

named:tank_source/content/2.annotation: Storage pressure (for compressed gases). Unit: "bar" or "psi". Example: 350 bar for hydrogen, 200 bar for compressed air.
named:tank_source/content/2.name: pressure

named:tank_source/content/4.annotation: Flow characterization: how fluid exits the tank and at what rate. Defines delivery method (pressurized, regulated, pumped, gravity), outlet pressure, max/peak flow rates, and regulation mechanism. Without this, the tank is just a capacity number with no delivery information.
named:tank_source/content/4.name: flow

named:track_surface/content/2.annotation: Ground pressure (vehicle weight / total track contact area). Unit: "kPa". Lower = better soft terrain performance.
named:track_surface/content/2.name: ground-pressure

named:transmission/content/0.annotation: Motor endpoint(s) driving this transmission, slash-path "comp_name/motor_name" (or a bare motor name when document-unique). A simple reduction has ONE motor; a differential coupling has TWO motor endpoints (use role="input" to disambiguate which motor drives which output).
named:transmission/content/0.name: motor

named:transmission/content/1.annotation: Joint endpoint(s) this transmission drives, by joint name. A simple reduction has ONE joint; a gearbox couples TWO joint endpoints (role="reference" plus role="driven") geared by the reduction ratio; a differential has TWO joint outputs (role="output").
named:transmission/content/1.name: joint

named:transmission/content/2.annotation: Gear reduction ratio (motor_speed / joint_speed). Values greater than 1 indicate speed reduction / torque multiplication. For example, 100 means the motor turns 100 times for each joint revolution.
named:transmission/content/2.name: reduction

named:transmission/content/3.annotation: Mechanical efficiency of the transmission as a fraction in [0, 1]. 1.0 = lossless, 0.9 = 90% efficient. Accounts for friction losses in gears, belts, and bearings.
named:transmission/content/3.name: efficiency

named:transmission/content/4.annotation: Mechanical backlash (dead zone) at the joint output. Unit: typically "rad" for rotary or "m" for linear transmissions.
named:transmission/content/4.name: backlash

named:transmission/content/5.annotation: Compliant spring element(s) in the drivetrain. Zero springs = rigid actuator. One series spring = SEA. One parallel spring = PEA. One of each = SEA+PEA combination. Springs with clutch/equilibrium-actuator/stiffness-actuator attributes express CPEA, AE-PEA, and VSA architectures respectively.
named:transmission/content/5.name: spring

named:transmission_spring/content/0.annotation: Spring stiffness (rate). Unit: "Nm/rad" for rotary, "N/m" for linear. For fixed-stiffness springs (SEA, PEA, CPEA, AE-PEA): specify the text content as the single stiffness value. For variable-stiffness actuators (VSA): use min and max attributes for the adjustable range. Example: 4.5 Nm/rad for HEBI X8-9 SEA, or min="5" max="500" unit="Nm/rad" for a VSA. This is the defining parameter of a compliant actuator: it determines force control bandwidth, impact energy absorption, and torque measurement resolution (torque = stiffness x deflection).
named:transmission_spring/content/0.name: stiffness

named:transmission_spring/content/1.annotation: Maximum spring deflection before mechanical hard stop. Unit: "rad" for rotary, "m" for linear. Defines the torque saturation limit: max_torque = stiffness x max_deflection. Beyond this deflection the actuator behaves rigidly. Example: 0.15 rad for a typical SEA torsion spring. Also determines maximum stored elastic energy: E = 0.5 x stiffness x max_deflection^2.
named:transmission_spring/content/1.name: max-deflection

named:transmission_spring/content/2.annotation: Viscous damping in the spring element. Unit: "Nm.s/rad" for rotary, "N.s/m" for linear. Most springs have minimal inherent damping; this captures any intentional damping added to the compliant element. Affects oscillation settling time and force control stability.
named:transmission_spring/content/2.name: damping

named:transmission_spring/content/3.annotation: Fixed spring rest position (equilibrium point) for PEA configurations. Unit: "rad" for rotary, "m" for linear. The joint angle at which the parallel spring exerts zero force. Typically tuned to the most common operating posture for optimal gravity compensation. For AE-PEA (adjustable equilibrium), use equilibrium-range instead.
named:transmission_spring/content/3.name: equilibrium

named:transmission_spring/content/4.annotation: Adjustable equilibrium range for AE-PEA configurations. Unit: "rad" for rotary, "m" for linear. min and max define the range over which the equilibrium motor can shift the spring rest position. The equilibrium-actuator attribute identifies the motor that performs this adjustment. Example: min="-1.57" max="0.0" for a knee joint that needs gravity compensation anywhere from full flexion to standing.
named:transmission_spring/content/4.name: equilibrium-range

named:transmission_spring/content/5.annotation: Electrical power required to operate the clutch mechanism for CPEA configurations. Unit: "W". For electromagnetic clutches: power to hold engaged (typically 1-5W). For mechanical latches: power for the actuation pulse only (zero holding power). Only applicable when the clutch attribute is set.
named:transmission_spring/content/5.name: clutch-power

named:transmission_spring/content/6.annotation: Clutch engagement/disengagement latency for CPEA configurations. Unit: "ms". Time from command to full engagement. Electromagnetic clutches: 2-10 ms. Mechanical latches: 10-50 ms. Affects how quickly the system can switch between compliant and rigid behavior (e.g., switching between stance and swing phase in walking).
named:transmission_spring/content/6.name: engage-time

named:urdf_compat_joint/content/0.annotation: URDF safety_controller, preserved for round-trip. Only meaningful on joints that map to URDF revolute/prismatic.
named:urdf_compat_joint/content/0.name: safety_controller

named:visual/content/0.annotation: Pose of the visual relative to the component origin (xyz/rpy or quat attributes; meters and radians). Default: identity (no offset).
named:visual/content/0.name: pose

named:visual/content/1.annotation: The appearance decision -- an EXCLUSIVE choice so a visual has a single source of truth (glTF-style; avoids the URDF/SDF mesh-vs-material ambiguity). ARM A: a self-contained GLB/glTF <model> (geometry + baked PBR/textures, content-addressed by @sha) -- NO <color> is grammatically reachable here, so a flat color can never fight the baked appearance; an optional primitive <geometry> may follow as a pure load-failure fallback. ARM B: a primitive <geometry> with an OPTIONAL flat <color> (inline RGBA or a named document-level color ref). A flat color is reachable ONLY on a primitive, so "GLB + color" is structurally impossible.

named:visual/content/1/0/0.annotation: Self-contained GLB/glTF asset (geometry + baked PBR/textures + node graph), content-addressed by @sha. THE rich-appearance form, the single source of truth for this visual; it carries no external color. A *visual* mesh is always this (GLB-only).
named:visual/content/1/0/0.name: model

named:visual/content/1/0/1.annotation: Optional primitive fallback, rendered only if the GLB model cannot be loaded.
named:visual/content/1/0/1.name: geometry

named:visual/content/1/1/0.annotation: Primitive shape (no baked appearance). For a mesh visual, use the GLB <model> arm instead.
named:visual/content/1/1/0.name: geometry

named:visual/content/1/1/1.annotation: Optional flat color for the primitive -- inline @rgba, or @name referencing a document-level color. The ONLY place a flat color may appear -- never alongside a GLB <model>.
named:visual/content/1/1/1.name: color

inline:root:hcdf.annotation: Root element of an HCDF cyber-physical robot description. Every HCDF file is a self-describing module: standalone robot descriptions and reusable sub-assemblies (arms, sensor heads, wheel modules) all use the same root element with the same metadata. When files are composed via include, each file retains its own name, author, and license, allowing tooling to trace provenance per sub-assembly and generate accurate bills of materials. Contains metadata, components, joints, joint groups, named kinematic states, self-collision configuration, physical connection assemblies, bindings, mates, topology objects, stream-profile references, transmissions, colors, and model-composition includes.

attributes.annotation: Name of the robot, platform, or sub-assembly described by this file. Required. For top-level robot descriptions, this is the robot's model name (e.g., "cogni-humanoid-v2", "quadrotor-x500"). For reusable sub-assemblies, this is the module name (e.g., "7dof-arm", "stereo-head-v2", "hebi-x8-9"). When a file is imported via include, the include's name attribute provides the instance name (e.g., "left_arm"), while this attribute provides the module identity. Use lowercase-with-hyphens by convention.
attributes.name: name

attributes.annotation: HCDF schema version this file conforms to. Current: 1.0. Pattern-validated MAJOR.MINOR. Core XSD validation is ordered and closed: unknown core elements are rejected, and domain-specific content belongs inside <extension>. Typed-loader compatibility is defined by the loader's version policy. Tooling binds to the embedded canonical hcdf.xsd by content SHA-256, not by this string alone.
attributes.name: version

attributes.annotation: Body-frame axis convention for all pose values in this file. FLU (X-forward, Y-left, Z-up): common in ground robotics and humanoid platforms. FRD (X-forward, Y-right, Z-down): common in aerospace and flight controllers. All xyz and rpy values in this document are expressed in the specified body-frame convention. Optional; when omitted, consumers should not assume a default and must either infer from context or require explicit specification. Semantic rule: all files in an include chain must use the same body-frame.
attributes.name: body-frame

attributes.annotation: World-frame (navigation/map frame) axis convention for global coordinates. ENU (X-east, Y-north, Z-up): common in GIS, surveying, and ground robotics. NED (X-north, Y-east, Z-down): common in aerospace, marine navigation, and flight controllers. Determines how global poses, waypoints, and map-relative coordinates are interpreted. Independent of body-frame. Optional; when omitted, consumers should not assume a default. Semantic rule: all files in an include chain must use the same world-frame.
attributes.name: world-frame

named:AudioSensorType.annotation: Audio/acoustic sensor sub-type. microphone: audio capture for speech, sound localization, acoustic monitoring. ultrasonic: ultrasonic transducer for proximity sensing and ranging (typically 40kHz). sonar: underwater acoustic ranging and imaging. hydrophone: underwater passive acoustic sensor for listening.
named:AudioSensorType.name: AudioSensorType

named:AxisValue.annotation: Sensor axis alignment mapping. Maps a sensor's internal axis to the component's body frame axis. Supports positive and negative directions: X, -X, Y, -Y, Z, -Z. Used to correct for sensors mounted in non-standard orientations.
named:AxisValue.name: AxisValue

named:BodyFrame.annotation: Body-frame axis convention describing how the robot's local coordinate axes are oriented relative to its physical body. The three-letter code specifies the direction each axis points: first letter = X, second = Y, third = Z. F=Forward, B=Back, L=Left, R=Right, U=Up, D=Down. FLU (X-forward, Y-left, Z-up): common in ground robotics, humanoids, and wheeled platforms. Positive X faces the direction the robot drives or walks. FRD (X-forward, Y-right, Z-down): common in aerospace, aviation, and flight controllers. Matches the aircraft body-frame convention where Z points toward the ground. Choosing a convention affects how all pose xyz and rpy values in the document are interpreted. Semantic rule for composition: all files in an include chain must use the same body-frame convention. Tooling should validate this at include-resolve time.
named:BodyFrame.name: BodyFrame

named:CameraDistortionModel.annotation: Distortion model naming the meaning of the camera_distortion coefficient set, matching ROS CameraInfo/distortion_model. plumb_bob: the classic 5-coefficient Brown-Conrady radial/tangential model (k1 k2 p1 p2 k3). rational_polynomial: the 8-coefficient rational model (k1 k2 p1 p2 k3 k4 k5 k6) for wide-angle lenses. equidistant: the 4-coefficient fisheye/Kannala-Brandt model (k1..k4 used as fisheye terms). Absent => assume plumb_bob.
named:CameraDistortionModel.name: CameraDistortionModel

named:CameraProjectionType.annotation: Lens projection model: how world-ray angles map to image-plane radius, which the Brown-Conrady camera_distortion coefficients CANNOT express for wide-angle/fisheye optics. pinhole: rectilinear (gnomonical) projection r = f*tan(theta); the standard perspective model the intrinsics/distortion already assume. stereographic: r = 2f*tan(theta/2), conformal. equidistant: r = f*theta, constant angular resolution (common fisheye). equisolid: r = 2f*sin(theta/2), equal-area (many circular fisheyes). orthographic: r = f*sin(theta), 180deg hemispherical. custom: mapping given by the custom-function coefficients. theta is the angle from the optical axis; f is focal length.
named:CameraProjectionType.name: CameraProjectionType

named:ChemicalSensorType.annotation: Chemical/environmental sensor sub-type. gas: gas concentration sensor (CO2, VOC, methane, etc.). ph: pH sensor for liquid acidity measurement. humidity: relative humidity sensor.
named:ChemicalSensorType.name: ChemicalSensorType

named:CompRole.annotation: Functional role of a component in the robot. sensor: sensing-only device (e.g., camera module, IMU board). compute: processing unit (e.g., SoC, SBC, FPGA). actuator: motor driver or actuator assembly. parent: structural/mechanical parent that groups child components (e.g., chassis, arm segment).
named:CompRole.name: CompRole

named:EmSensorType.annotation: Near-field electromagnetic sensor sub-type. Measures static or quasi-static EM fields, NOT propagating radio waves (those are rf). mag: magnetometer (measures Earth's magnetic field or local fields). metal_detector: inductive proximity sensing. eddy_current: non-destructive testing via induced currents. emf: electromotive force measurement. hall-effect: Hall effect proximity/position sensor. fluxgate: fluxgate magnetometer (high-precision compass).
named:EmSensorType.name: EmSensorType

named:EncoderPrinciple.annotation: Physical sensing principle of the encoder. optical: light source + photodetector + code disk (e.g., US Digital, Broadcom AEDR). magnetic: Hall effect or magnetoresistive element + rotating magnet (e.g., AS5048A, AS5600). inductive: resolver, electromagnetic induction between coils. capacitive: capacitance change between rotating plates. resistive: potentiometer, resistance proportional to position.
named:EncoderPrinciple.name: EncoderPrinciple

named:EncoderSensorType.annotation: Encoder measurement type. incremental: relative position from index/home, requires homing. absolute: absolute position within one revolution (single-turn) or multiple revolutions (multi-turn). linear: linear position encoder (e.g., optical strip, magnetic linear).
named:EncoderSensorType.name: EncoderSensorType

named:FluidSensorType.annotation: Fluid sensor sub-type: the measurand is fluid (gas or liquid) pressure or flow, as distinct from force (solid/mechanical contact loads) and chemical (composition). Application sub-types: barometer (absolute atmospheric pressure, derives altitude), airspeed (differential/dynamic pressure from a pitot probe, derives airspeed), depth (hydrostatic pressure, derives submersion depth), flow (volumetric or mass flow rate), level (liquid level via hydrostatic head). Reference-mode sub-types (name the pressure reference of a general-purpose transducer): differential (across two ports), gauge (relative to ambient), absolute (relative to vacuum), sealed (relative to a sealed reference, typically 1 atm), vacuum (below-ambient/vacuum measurement). Choose the application sub-type when the device has a defined purpose; choose the reference-mode sub-type for a general-purpose pressure transducer.
named:FluidSensorType.name: FluidSensorType

named:ForceFrame.annotation: Reference frame in which a force/torque sensor reports its wrench, matching SDF force_torque/frame. parent: the joint parent link frame. child: the joint child link frame. sensor: the sensor's own frame. Absent => the simulator/hardware default (SDF defaults to "child").
named:ForceFrame.name: ForceFrame

named:ForceSensorType.annotation: Force/torque sensor sub-type. strain: strain gauge for deformation measurement. pressure: pressure transducer (barometric or contact). torque: rotary torque sensor. load_cell: load cell for weight/force measurement.
named:ForceSensorType.name: ForceSensorType

named:FrustumShape.annotation: Cross-section shape of a frustum used for sensor field-of-view visualization.
named:FrustumShape.name: FrustumShape

named:HcdfVersion.annotation: HCDF schema version as MAJOR.MINOR (e.g. "1.0"). Validating pattern (replaces the former unvalidated xs:string) so a document declaring an unknown version shape is rejected, and same-version-string drift is caught by binding the converter to the canonical hcdf.xsd by content hash.
named:HcdfVersion.name: HcdfVersion

named:HmiType.annotation: Human-Machine Interface element type. display: visual output (LCD, OLED, LED matrix, e-ink). speaker: audio output (speaker, buzzer, piezo). led-status: status indicator LED(s) (on/off, color). led-illumination: scene illumination (headlights, work lights, IR illumination for night vision cameras). button: physical pushbutton or switch input. touchscreen: combined display + touch input. indicator: generic visual/audio indicator.
named:HmiType.name: HmiType

named:InertialSensorType.annotation: Inertial sensor sub-type. accel: accelerometer only (3-axis linear acceleration). gyro: gyroscope only (3-axis angular rate). accel_gyro: combined IMU with both accelerometer and gyroscope (6-axis).
named:InertialSensorType.name: InertialSensorType

named:JointType.annotation: Enumeration of kinematic joint types. revolute: bounded single-axis rotation (requires axis + limit; radians/Nm). continuous: unbounded single-axis rotation (requires axis; limit is optional and carries effort/velocity ONLY; lower/upper are forbidden). prismatic: bounded linear translation (sliding; requires axis + limit; meters/N). fixed: rigid (zero DOF; axis and limit forbidden). ball: 3-DOF spherical (swing-cone + independent twist; axis, axis2, limit, limit2, and thread_pitch are all forbidden). universal: 2-DOF (requires axis + axis2; limit bounds the primary axis and limit2 bounds axis2, both radians). planar: 2-DOF translation on a plane (requires axis = the plane normal; limit and limit2 are the two in-plane translation ranges, meters). screw: helical, 1-DOF (requires axis + thread_pitch; limit bounds the ROTATIONAL DOF in radians and the coupled axial translation is derived via thread_pitch: canonical pitch is meters-per-revolution, right-handed). cylindrical: 2-DOF rotation + translation on the same axis (like a piston that can also rotate; requires axis + limit; limit is the translation range in meters and limit2, when present, is the rotation range in radians; the rotation bound is optional). free: 6-DOF unconstrained (all translation and rotation allowed, used for the root body of mobile robots, free-flying spacecraft, and any body not kinematically constrained to a parent; axis and limit are forbidden).
named:JointType.name: JointType

named:MeasureDirection.annotation: Sign convention for the wrench a force/torque sensor reports, matching SDF force_torque/measure_direction. parent_to_child: the wrench the parent applies to the child. child_to_parent: the wrench the child applies to the parent (the negation). Absent => the simulator default (SDF defaults to "child_to_parent"). Flipping this negates the reported force and torque.
named:MeasureDirection.name: MeasureDirection

named:MotorType.annotation: Motor or actuator technology type. bldc: brushless DC motor. brushed: brushed DC motor. stepper: stepper motor. servo: hobby/industrial servo. linear: linear actuator (proportional control over stroke length). solenoid: electromagnetic on/off linear actuator (binary pull/push action with no proportional position control, used for valves, latches, locks, pin releases, landing gear, and gripper release mechanisms). hydraulic: hydraulic actuator. pneumatic: pneumatic actuator. thrust: thrust motor (propeller, jet, rocket). ice: internal combustion engine (gasoline, diesel; for generators or direct mechanical drive).
named:MotorType.name: MotorType

named:NameOrigin.annotation: Provenance of a visual/collision name: "authored" = meaningful, human/source-supplied (round-trips, emitted to URDF where the URDF schema allows it); "synthesized" = generated by a converter to satisfy HCDF's required-name rule (stripped on URDF export so the output stays byte-clean). Absence is interpreted as "authored" by the companion validator.
named:NameOrigin.name: NameOrigin

named:NoiseType.annotation: Noise distribution model for sensor simulation. gaussian: Gaussian (normal) distribution with mean and stddev. uniform: uniform distribution over a range. none: no noise applied (ideal sensor).
named:NoiseType.name: NoiseType

named:OpticalSensorType.annotation: Optical sensor sub-type. camera: visible-spectrum image sensor (RGB, mono, stereo, depth). thermal: infrared thermal camera (LWIR/MWIR). lidar: Light Detection and Ranging (spinning or solid-state). tof: Time-of-Flight depth sensor. optical_flow: optical flow sensor for velocity estimation.
named:OpticalSensorType.name: OpticalSensorType

named:ProbeType.annotation: Flow/velocity probe geometry for a fluid sensor (airspeed or flow sub-types). pitot: single total-pressure tube; static pressure taken from a separate source. pitot_static: combined Prandtl tube carrying both total and static ports. multihole: multi-port probe (e.g. 5-hole/7-hole) resolving flow angle as well as speed. hotwire: thermal anemometer (heated element, convective cooling proportional to speed). venturi: venturi/nozzle differential-pressure flow element. orifice: orifice-plate differential-pressure flow element.
named:ProbeType.name: ProbeType

named:Quat4.annotation: Orientation quaternion as exactly four space-separated doubles "x y z w" (Hamilton convention, scalar-last). The fixed length-4 list rejects malformed 3- or 7-value strings that the former bare xs:string allowed.
named:Quat4.name: Quat4

named:RadiationSensorType.annotation: Radiation sensor sub-type for nuclear inspection, environmental monitoring, and space robotics. geiger: Geiger-Muller tube for ionizing radiation counting (alpha, beta, gamma). scintillation: scintillation detector for gamma spectroscopy (higher energy resolution than Geiger). neutron: neutron detector for nuclear material detection. dosimeter: cumulative radiation dose measurement.
named:RadiationSensorType.name: RadiationSensorType

named:RfSensorType.annotation: Radio-frequency sensor sub-type. Uses propagating radio waves for ranging, positioning, or imaging; distinct from em which measures static/quasi-static fields. gnss: satellite navigation receiver. uwb: Ultra-Wideband ranging. radar: radio detection and ranging (24/77/79 GHz). radio_altimeter: radio altitude measurement.
named:RfSensorType.name: RfSensorType

named:RoleType.annotation: Role of an endpoint within a MULTI-ENDPOINT transmission coupling, disambiguating which motor drives which output and how outputs are geared together. Omit for a simple single-motor/single-joint reduction, where each endpoint's part is unambiguous. reference: the fixed reference endpoint a driven endpoint is geared against (a gearbox's reference joint/body). driven: the output endpoint driven through the coupling relative to the reference (a gearbox's driven joint). input: an input endpoint of the coupling (a differential's motor inputs). output: an output endpoint of the coupling (a differential's joint outputs).
named:RoleType.name: RoleType

named:TactileSensorType.annotation: Tactile sensor sub-type. Tactile sensors measure contact, pressure, or deformation distributed across a surface area, as distinct from force sensors which measure at a single point. capacitive: measures pressure via capacitance change between conductive layers; high sensitivity, good spatial resolution, common in robot fingertips and e-skin (e.g., PPS TakkTile, SynTouch BioTac). resistive: force-sensitive resistor (FSR) arrays or piezoresistive films; lower cost, simpler electronics, used in gripper pads and pressure mats (e.g., Interlink FSR, Tekscan FlexiForce). piezoelectric: generates voltage from mechanical deformation; measures dynamic contact events (slip, vibration, texture) rather than static pressure, used for slip detection in dexterous hands. barometric: array of barometric pressure sensors under a deformable membrane; robust to wear, high dynamic range, used in soft grippers and compliant fingers (e.g., XELA uSkin). optical: uses internal cameras and deformable gel to measure contact geometry via image analysis; provides rich 3D contact shape and shear force data (e.g., GelSight, DIGIT, GelSlim).
named:TactileSensorType.name: TactileSensorType

named:TemperatureSensorType.annotation: Temperature sensor type. thermistor: NTC or PTC resistive element (common in motors for winding temp). rtd: Resistance Temperature Detector (PT100/PT1000, high accuracy). thermocouple: K/J/T/E type junction (wide range, industrial). ir: non-contact infrared temperature sensor.
named:TemperatureSensorType.name: TemperatureSensorType

named:TransmissionType.annotation: Mechanical power transmission mechanism between motor and joint. simple: direct drive or single-stage reduction. differential: differential gear mechanism (couples two motors to two outputs). belt: belt/pulley transmission. gear: spur or helical gear train. planetary: planetary (epicyclic) gear set (compact, high ratio). cycloidal: cycloidal drive (high ratio, zero backlash, high shock load capacity, used in robot joints). harmonic: harmonic drive / strain-wave gearing (very high ratio in compact form, used in robot arms; Harmonic Drive AG). strain-wave: same as harmonic (alternate name). worm: worm gear (high ratio, self-locking, lower efficiency, used where back-driving prevention needed).
named:TransmissionType.name: TransmissionType

named:WorldFrame.annotation: World-frame (navigation frame) axis convention describing how global/map coordinate axes are oriented. ENU (X-east, Y-north, Z-up): common in geographic information systems, ground robotics, and surveying. Z-up aligns with gravity opposition, making vertical reasoning intuitive. NED (X-north, Y-east, Z-down): common in aerospace, aviation, marine navigation, and most inertial navigation systems. Z-down aligns with gravity direction, matching accelerometer sign conventions in flight controllers. The world-frame convention determines how global poses, waypoints, and map coordinates are interpreted. Independent of body-frame: a ground robot may use body-frame=FLU with world-frame=ENU, while a drone may use body-frame=FRD with world-frame=NED. Semantic rule for composition: all files in an include chain must use the same world-frame convention.
named:WorldFrame.name: WorldFrame

named:aerofoil_surface.annotation: Aerodynamic lifting surface (wing, horizontal stabilizer, canard). Generates lift and drag from airflow over an airfoil cross-section. Key parameters determine flight performance: lift coefficient, stall characteristics, and induced drag.
named:aerofoil_surface.name: aerofoil_surface

named:audio_sensor.annotation: Audio/acoustic sensor for sound capture, ultrasonic ranging, and underwater acoustics. Can be a passive receiver (microphone, hydrophone) or an active transducer (ultrasonic, sonar) that emits and receives. Extends sensor_base with audio type attribute and optional frequency/directivity parameters.

attributes.annotation: Audio sensor type (microphone, ultrasonic, sonar, hydrophone). Required.
attributes.name: type

attributes.annotation: Whether this is an active transducer (emits and receives) or passive (receives only). true for ultrasonic/sonar emitter+receiver pairs; false for microphones and hydrophones.
attributes.name: active

named:audio_sensor.name: audio_sensor

named:axis.annotation: Joint axis of rotation or translation. Defines the direction vector along or around which the joint moves, expressed in the joint's local frame.

attributes.annotation: Axis direction vector as three space-separated doubles "x y z". Does not need to be unit-length (will be normalized). Default: "1 0 0" (X axis). Examples: "0 0 1" for Z-axis rotation, "0 1 0" for Y-axis.
attributes.name: xyz

named:axis.name: axis

named:axis_align.annotation: Axis alignment mapping from a sensor's internal coordinate frame to the component's body frame. Used to correct for sensors mounted in non-standard orientations without changing the pose.

attributes.annotation: Which body-frame axis the sensor's X axis maps to. Default: X (no remapping).
attributes.name: x

attributes.annotation: Which body-frame axis the sensor's Y axis maps to. Default: Y (no remapping).
attributes.name: y

attributes.annotation: Which body-frame axis the sensor's Z axis maps to. Default: Z (no remapping).
attributes.name: z

named:axis_align.name: axis_align

named:axis_noise.annotation: Independent noise model for each of the x, y, and z channels of a 3-axis measurement. Each child is a full <noise> model. Optional per-axis override of a scalar <noise> that applies to all axes; present when a datasheet or simulator specifies anisotropic per-axis noise (SDF gz-sim per-axis <noise> blocks).
named:axis_noise.name: axis_noise

named:battery_source.annotation: Rechargeable battery energy source. Defines cell configuration, chemistry, capacity, and discharge limits. An agent uses this to compute runtime (energy / total power consumption) and validate that bus voltage stays within all consumers' operating range throughout discharge.
named:battery_source.name: battery_source

named:box.annotation: Axis-aligned box geometry primitive centered at the parent pose origin.
named:box.name: box

named:camera_binning.annotation: Pixel binning factors (ROS CameraInfo binning_x/binning_y). 1 = no binning; 2 = every 2x2 block combined into one output pixel.

attributes.annotation: Horizontal binning factor (CameraInfo/binning_x).
attributes.name: x

attributes.annotation: Vertical binning factor (CameraInfo/binning_y).
attributes.name: y

named:camera_binning.name: camera_binning

named:camera_calibration.annotation: Camera calibration results from an actual calibration procedure on a specific unit. Distinct from the design-spec intrinsics/distortion: those are nominal datasheet values, while calibration contains measured values for this particular camera+lens assembly. An agent doing visual servoing, SLAM, or stereo depth must use the calibrated values. If calibration is present, it overrides the design-spec intrinsics and distortion for runtime use.
named:camera_calibration.name: camera_calibration

named:camera_distortion.annotation: Camera lens distortion parameters following the Brown-Conrady model. Used by vision pipelines to undistort images.

attributes.annotation: Distortion model naming the coefficient-set meaning (ROS CameraInfo/distortion_model): plumb_bob (5-coeff Brown-Conrady, the default), rational_polynomial (8-coeff k1..k6+p1p2), or equidistant (4-coeff fisheye). Optional; absent => plumb_bob.
attributes.name: model

named:camera_distortion.name: camera_distortion

named:camera_intrinsics.annotation: Camera intrinsic parameters following the pinhole camera model. Defines image dimensions, pixel format, and focal length/principal point for projection calculations.
named:camera_intrinsics.name: camera_intrinsics

named:camera_lens.annotation: Lens projection model for a camera field-of-view. Complements camera_intrinsics (the pinhole K matrix) and camera_distortion (Brown-Conrady radial/tangential terms, valid only for near-rectilinear lenses). A fisheye or other wide-angle lens is NOT describable by Brown-Conrady coefficients; this element names the projection function (equidistant, equisolid, stereographic, orthographic, or a custom mapping) and the field cutoff so a perception pipeline can unproject correctly. Maps to SDF camera/lens (type, cutoff_angle, scale_to_hfov, custom_function). Absent lens => assume pinhole/rectilinear per the intrinsics.

attributes.annotation: Projection model (pinhole, stereographic, equidistant, equisolid, orthographic, custom). Required when a lens element is present.
attributes.name: type

named:camera_lens.name: camera_lens

named:camera_matrix.annotation: Full ROS CameraInfo geometry beyond the pinhole K matrix (which lives in <intrinsics>) and the D coefficients (in <distortion>): the rectification matrix R, the projection matrix P, and the pixel binning + region-of-interest. Present for a stereo-rectified or cropped/binned camera whose runtime projection differs from the raw intrinsics. All children optional; absent => identity rectification, projection = K, no binning, full-frame ROI.
named:camera_matrix.name: camera_matrix

named:camera_params.annotation: Camera-specific parameters affecting perception pipeline design, bandwidth planning, and environmental capability. Applies to optical sensors with type="camera" or type="thermal".
named:camera_params.name: camera_params

named:camera_projection.annotation: Structured ROS CameraInfo projection matrix P (3x4) = [[fx' 0 cx' Tx],[0 fy' cy' Ty],[0 0 1 0]]. The rectified intrinsics (fx'/fy'/cx'/cy') plus the stereo baseline translation (tx = -fx'*baseline for the right camera, ty for vertical stereo).
named:camera_projection.name: camera_projection

named:camera_roi.annotation: Region of interest sub-window (ROS CameraInfo/RegionOfInterest): the captured rectangle within the full sensor, plus whether it applies before or after rectification.

attributes.annotation: Leftmost pixel column of the ROI (CameraInfo/roi/x_offset). Default 0.
attributes.name: x-offset

attributes.annotation: Topmost pixel row of the ROI (CameraInfo/roi/y_offset). Default 0.
attributes.name: y-offset

attributes.annotation: ROI width in pixels (CameraInfo/roi/width). 0 => full width.
attributes.name: width

attributes.annotation: ROI height in pixels (CameraInfo/roi/height). 0 => full height.
attributes.name: height

attributes.annotation: Whether a distinct ROI rectification is required (CameraInfo/roi/do_rectify).
attributes.name: rectify

named:camera_roi.name: camera_roi

named:capsule.annotation: Capsule (cylinder with hemispherical caps) geometry primitive, aligned with the Z axis. Total height = length + 2 * radius.
named:capsule.name: capsule

named:chemical_sensor.annotation: Chemical/environmental sensor (gas detector, pH sensor, humidity sensor). Extends sensor_base with all common elements.

attributes.annotation: Chemical sensor sub-type (gas, ph, humidity). Required.
attributes.name: type

named:chemical_sensor.name: chemical_sensor

named:collision.annotation: Collision geometry for physics simulation and proximity detection. Typically a simplified version of the visual geometry (bounding box, convex hull, or low-poly mesh). Multiple collision elements per component are allowed for complex shapes.

attributes.annotation: Unique name for this collision shape within the component. Required.
attributes.name: name

attributes.annotation: Provenance of the name (authored vs converter-synthesized). Optional; absence means authored. URDF collision @name is optional, so an unnamed URDF collision imports as "synthesized" and is stripped on export.
attributes.name: name-origin

attributes.annotation: URDF-compat: the per-collision URDF <verbose> flag (zero CPS meaning), kept per-collision (not on the comp-level urdf-compat) so each collision round-trips its own flag. Optional; omit for native HCDF.
attributes.name: verbose

named:collision.name: collision

named:collision_geometry.annotation: Collision geometry: primitive shapes (box, cylinder, sphere, capsule, cone, ellipsoid) plus an external <mesh>. Prefer primitives or a convex hull for efficiency; a collision <mesh> should be a LEAN format (STL/OBJ/DAE/convex), NOT a GLB -- collision needs shape, not baked appearance (validator-enforced; URI format is not XSD-expressible). Frustum is excluded (sensor-FOV only). Carries no material (collision has no appearance).
named:collision_geometry.name: collision_geometry

named:collision_pair.annotation: A pair of components to skip for self-collision checking. Adjacent links, links on opposite sides of the robot, and always-in-contact pairs are common candidates.

attributes.annotation: First component name.
attributes.name: comp1

attributes.annotation: Second component name.
attributes.name: comp2

attributes.annotation: Why this pair is disabled: "adjacent" (share a joint), "unreachable" (physically can't collide), "mounted" (always in contact by design). Optional documentation.
attributes.name: reason

named:collision_pair.name: collision_pair

named:color.annotation: RGBA appearance color. Used three ways: (1) DEFINE a reusable color at document level with @name + @rgba; (2) REFERENCE a document-level color from a visual by @name alone; (3) INLINE a one-off color with @rgba alone. This is HCDF's flat-appearance tier (the URDF-portable color); rich appearance (PBR/textures) is baked into the GLB <model>, never expressed here. There is no separate <material> element -- a color is the appearance unit, and contact physics lives independently on <collision><surface>.

attributes.annotation: Optional. At document level, declares a reusable color by this name (must be unique). On a visual, either references a document-level color by name (omit @rgba) or names a one-off inline color. Maps to/from URDF's <material name> wrapper.
attributes.name: name

attributes.annotation: Four space-separated floats "R G B A" each in [0, 1]. R=red, G=green, B=blue, A=alpha (1=opaque, 0=transparent). Default: "0 0 0 1" (opaque black). Omit when referencing a named color by @name alone.
attributes.name: rgba

attributes.annotation: Optional human-readable note (e.g., "carbon fiber", "anodized aluminum") -- carries intent when a color is named after a material/substance.
attributes.name: description

named:color.name: color

named:comp.annotation: A component representing a rigid body or hardware assembly. Contains physical properties (inertial, visual, collision), functional ports and network functions, physical connectors, antennas, sensors, motors, firmware identity, and runtime discovery state. Equivalent to URDF's link element but extended with connectivity and cyber-physical infrastructure.

attributes.annotation: Unique name for this component (e.g., "spine_soc", "left_shoulder", "wheel_fl_motor_driver"). Required. Used in joint parent/child references, port paths, and chain hop references.
attributes.name: name

attributes.annotation: Functional role (sensor, compute, actuator, parent). Optional. Aids tooling in categorizing components for network planning and visualization.
attributes.name: role

attributes.annotation: Hardware identifier for matching physical devices during discovery (e.g., serial number, MAC address prefix, or part number). Optional. Used by discovery agents to map physical hardware to HCDF components.
attributes.name: hwid

attributes.annotation: Structural classification of this component: fuselage, wing, boom, mast, hull, chassis, frame, arm, leg, tail, nacelle, pod. Optional; provides semantic context for the component's role in the robot's body architecture. Used by agents for high-level reasoning about robot morphology.
attributes.name: struct-type

attributes.annotation: Ingress Protection rating per IEC 60529 (e.g., "IP67", "IP68", "IP54") or NEMA enclosure type (e.g., "NEMA-4X", "NEMA-6P"). The two-digit IP code indicates protection against solids (first digit, 0-6) and liquids (second digit, 0-9K): IP54 = dust-protected + splash-proof. IP65 = dust-tight + water jets. IP67 = dust-tight + temporary immersion (1m, 30min). IP68 = dust-tight + continuous immersion (depth/duration defined by manufacturer). IP69K = dust-tight + high-pressure steam cleaning. An agent uses this to validate that all components meet the environmental requirements for the target deployment (outdoor, underwater, washdown). Components without ip-rating are assumed to have no specific protection (or the rating is unknown). Optional; free-form string to support both IP and NEMA systems.
attributes.name: ip-rating

named:comp.name: comp

named:cone.annotation: Solid cone primitive. Base circle of given radius, tapering to a point at the given length along the Z axis. Use for nose cones, drill bits, funnels, pointed housings. Distinct from frustum which is a truncated cone for FOV visualization.
named:cone.name: cone

named:contact.annotation: Contact dynamics parameters for collision response in physics simulation.

attributes.annotation: Contact stiffness in N/m. Higher values create harder contacts with less penetration.
attributes.name: stiffness

attributes.annotation: Contact damping coefficient in N*s/m. Dissipates energy during contact to reduce bouncing.
attributes.name: damping

named:contact.name: contact

named:control_modes.annotation: Control interfaces supported by the motor. Determines how an agent can command this actuator: position (servo-like), velocity (speed control), torque/force (direct effort), current (low-level FOC).
named:control_modes.name: control_modes

named:control_surface_def.annotation: Aerodynamic control surface (aileron, elevon, elevator, rudder, flap, spoiler). A hinged portion of a wing or tail that deflects to change aerodynamic forces. The joint connecting this comp defines the hinge axis; this element defines the aerodynamic properties.

attributes.annotation: Control surface type: "aileron", "elevator", "rudder", "elevon", "flaperon", "flap", "spoiler", "canard", "ruddervator", "v-tail".
attributes.name: type

named:control_surface_def.name: control_surface_def

named:cylinder.annotation: Cylinder geometry primitive centered at the parent pose origin, aligned with the Z axis.
named:cylinder.name: cylinder

named:data_output.annotation: Sensor data output characteristics for network bandwidth planning. An agent uses this to validate that network links and TSN schedules can carry the sensor's data. Only relevant for high-bandwidth sensors (cameras, lidars, radars) that transmit over the network. Not needed for low-bandwidth sensors (IMU, baro, mag) connected via SPI/I2C.
named:data_output.name: data_output

named:discovered.annotation: Runtime discovery state for a component. Populated by device discovery agents (mDNS, LLDP, EtherCAT scan) at runtime. Not typically authored by hand: updated automatically by HCDF tooling after network scanning.
named:discovered.name: discovered

named:dynamic_surface.annotation: Dynamic surface that interacts with the environment (air, water, ground, or grasped objects). Includes aerodynamic surfaces (wings, control surfaces, propellers), hydrodynamic surfaces (hydrofoils), ground contact surfaces (wheels, tracks), and gripper contact surfaces (mechanical pads, suction cups, magnetic, adhesive). Each surface has a name and contains exactly one surface type definition. The comp's joints define the actuation (hinge axes, deflection); the surface defines the physical interaction properties.

attributes.annotation: Unique name for this surface within the component.
attributes.name: name

attributes.annotation: Name of the visual element containing this surface's mesh for 3D highlighting.
attributes.name: visual

attributes.annotation: GLTF mesh node name within the visual for 3D highlighting of this surface.
attributes.name: mesh

named:dynamic_surface.name: dynamic_surface

named:ellipsoid.annotation: Ellipsoid primitive defined by three semi-axis radii. A sphere is a special case where all three radii are equal. Use for approximating heads, torsos, drone fuselages, and other non-uniform rounded shapes. Supported by SDF.
named:ellipsoid.name: ellipsoid

named:em_sensor.annotation: Electromagnetic field sensor (magnetometer, metal detector, eddy current probe, EMF sensor). Extends sensor_base with all common elements (pose, driver, range, resolution, ODR, bandwidth, FIFO, noise, geometry).

attributes.annotation: Electromagnetic sensor sub-type (mag, metal_detector, eddy_current, emf). Required.
attributes.name: type

named:em_sensor.name: em_sensor

named:encoder_sensor.annotation: Position/velocity encoder sensor. Extends sensor_base with encoder-specific attributes: measurement type (incremental, absolute, linear), physical sensing principle (optical, magnetic, inductive, capacitive, resistive), and communication interface (quadrature, SSI, BiSS, EnDat, SPI). Can be mounted on a motor shaft, joint output, wheel, or linear axis. Motors and transmissions reference encoder sensors by name.

attributes.annotation: Encoder measurement type: incremental (relative, needs homing), absolute (absolute position per revolution or multi-turn), or linear. Required.
attributes.name: type

attributes.annotation: Physical sensing principle: optical, magnetic, inductive, capacitive, or resistive.
attributes.name: principle

attributes.annotation: Communication interface: quadrature, ssi, biss, endat, spi, analog.
attributes.name: interface

named:encoder_sensor.name: encoder_sensor

named:exclude_submesh.annotation: Names a sub-part (a node/group) inside a multi-part mesh to SUBTRACT from the loaded geometry: the whole model minus this subtree, the complement of <submesh>'s include. Used under <model> in exclude mode. Deliberately carries NO @center: recentering is meaningful only for a lone included piece, never for a subtraction, so an exclusion cannot even spell it (illegal by grammar rather than validator-caught).

attributes.annotation: Name of the sub-part (submesh/node) within the mesh file to subtract; the node and its whole subtree are removed from the loaded geometry. Required.
attributes.name: name

named:exclude_submesh.name: exclude_submesh

named:extension.annotation: Vendor or domain-specific extension container. Allows embedding arbitrary XML content from external domains (e.g., simulation parameters, vendor-specific configurations, CI/CD metadata) without modifying the HCDF core schema. Content is processed with lax validation.

attributes.annotation: Namespace or domain identifier for the extension content (e.g., "gazebo", "isaac-sim", "vendor:mycompany", "ci:github-actions"). Required.
attributes.name: domain

attributes.annotation: Version of the extension schema for forward compatibility. Optional.
attributes.name: version

named:extension.name: extension

named:fifo_config.annotation: Hardware FIFO (First-In-First-Out) buffer configuration. Many sensors (IMUs, ADCs) collect samples into a hardware FIFO and trigger an interrupt when the watermark level is reached. This reduces interrupt overhead and allows burst processing. Effective update rate = ODR / watermark.

attributes.annotation: Maximum FIFO depth in samples (hardware limit, e.g., 256 for ICM45686, 512 for BMI088). This is the total buffer capacity before overflow.
attributes.name: depth

attributes.annotation: Watermark level in samples: interrupt fires when this many samples have accumulated. Controls the effective processing rate: effective_rate = ODR / watermark. Example: ODR=3200Hz, watermark=8 → 400Hz interrupt rate, 8 samples per burst.
attributes.name: watermark

named:fifo_config.name: fifo_config

named:flow_characterization.annotation: Flow characterization for a fuel/gas tank: how fluid exits the tank and at what rate. Without this, a tank is just a container; the flow characterization tells an agent how fast energy can be delivered to consumers. An agent uses this to compute: max power delivery (flow_rate x energy_density), surge capability (peak flow for acceleration transients), and runtime at load (volume x density / operating_flow_rate).
named:flow_characterization.name: flow_characterization

named:fluid_probe.annotation: Flow/velocity probe description for a fluid sensor (airspeed or flow sub-types). Records probe geometry and which pressure ports it exposes, so an agent can reason about installation (alignment into the flow) and which raw pressures are available.

attributes.annotation: Probe geometry (pitot, pitot_static, multihole, hotwire, venturi, orifice).
attributes.name: type

attributes.annotation: True if the probe provides a static-pressure port. A bare pitot has only a total port and needs an external static source; a pitot_static/Prandtl tube provides both.
attributes.name: static-port

attributes.annotation: True if the probe provides a total- (stagnation-) pressure port.
attributes.name: total-port

attributes.annotation: Number of pressure-sensing ports on the probe (e.g. 5 or 7 for a multihole probe). Optional.
attributes.name: ports

named:fluid_probe.name: fluid_probe

named:fluid_sensor.annotation: Fluid sensor: measures pressure or flow of a gas or liquid. The twelfth sensor category, distinct from force (solid/mechanical contact loads) and chemical (composition): the measurand here is fluid pressure/flow. Covers barometers (absolute atmospheric pressure -> altitude), airspeed/pitot sensors (differential dynamic pressure -> airspeed), depth sensors (hydrostatic pressure -> depth), flow meters, liquid-level sensors, and general-purpose differential/gauge/absolute/sealed/vacuum pressure transducers. Extends sensor_base, so pose, driver, the scalar resolution (here the pressure resolution), the noise model, data-output, and geometry are inherited; the group update-rate (sensor/@update-rate) gives the output rate. The children below add the pressure core, the reference values, the per-subtype derived outputs (altitude/airspeed/depth/level/flow), and the flow probe. All are optional; populate those relevant to the @type.

attributes.annotation: Fluid sensor sub-type (barometer, airspeed, depth, flow, level, differential, gauge, absolute, sealed, vacuum). Required. Determines which derived-output children (altitude/airspeed/depth/level/flow) and reference values apply.
attributes.name: type

named:fluid_sensor.name: fluid_sensor

named:force_axis_noise.annotation: Per-axis noise for a multi-axis force/torque sensor: an independent <noise> model on each force channel (force/x, force/y, force/z) and each torque channel (torque/x, torque/y, torque/z). Maps to the SDF force_torque per-axis force/torque <noise> blocks. Optional; complements the inherited scalar <noise> (which stays as the isotropic fallback).
named:force_axis_noise.name: force_axis_noise

named:force_sensor.annotation: Force/torque sensor (strain gauge, pressure transducer, torque sensor, load cell). Extends sensor_base with all common elements. A multi-axis force/torque sensor mounted on a joint additionally carries the reporting @frame and @measure-direction sign convention and optional per-axis noise; a contact sensor names the <collision> it monitors.

attributes.annotation: Force sensor sub-type (strain, pressure, torque, load_cell). Required.
attributes.name: type

attributes.annotation: Reference frame the wrench is reported in (parent/child/sensor). SDF force_torque/frame. Optional; absent => simulator default (child).
attributes.name: frame

attributes.annotation: Sign convention for the reported wrench (parent_to_child / child_to_parent). SDF force_torque/measure_direction. Optional; absent => simulator default (child_to_parent). Flipping this negates the reported force and torque.
attributes.name: measure-direction

named:force_sensor.name: force_sensor

named:frame.annotation: Named coordinate frame attached to a component. Used for expressing sensor mounts, tool center points, mounting holes, or any reference point that other elements can relate to via the relative-to attribute.

attributes.annotation: Unique name for this frame within the component. Required. Referenced by other elements using the frame name.
attributes.name: name

attributes.annotation: Name of the anchor this frame's pose is expressed relative to: a sibling frame (comp-local frame name), a comp (document-unique comp name -- including this frame's own comp, to state the component origin explicitly), or a joint (its joint frame). This mirrors SDF's frame graph, where a frame may attach to a link, joint, or frame. If omitted, the pose is relative to this frame's own component origin. Because the reference resolves against the UNION of frame, comp, and joint names -- a heterogeneous namespace an XSD keyref cannot target (a keyref binds exactly one key) -- referential integrity is enforced by the companion validator, not the schema. On a name collision, resolution precedence is: sibling frame (most local) > comp > joint.
attributes.name: relative-to

attributes.annotation: Frame purpose type: "tcp" (Tool Center Point for end-effector control), "sensor-origin" (sensor reference frame), "attachment" (mechanical mounting point), "optical" (camera optical frame, Z-forward convention). Optional; omit for general-purpose frames.
attributes.name: type

named:frame.name: frame

named:friction.annotation: Friction coefficients for contact simulation between surfaces.

attributes.annotation: Static friction coefficient (dimensionless). Force required to initiate sliding. Default: 0.
attributes.name: static

attributes.annotation: Dynamic (kinetic) friction coefficient (dimensionless). Force during sliding. Must be less than or equal to static. Default: 0.
attributes.name: dynamic

named:friction.name: friction

named:friction_direction.annotation: Anisotropic (direction-dependent) friction for a contact surface, matching SDF surface/friction/ode fdir1 + mu2 + slip1/slip2. The primary friction coefficient (friction/@static, and its kinetic counterpart @dynamic) acts along one principal direction; this element names the FIRST friction direction (fdir1) and the SECOND-direction coefficient (@mu2) plus per-direction slip compliance. Optional; present only for anisotropic surfaces (tires, tracks, directional ground). NOTE: @mu2 here is the true 2nd-DIRECTION coefficient (distinct from friction/@dynamic, which HCDF uses for the kinetic coefficient).

attributes.annotation: Friction coefficient in the SECOND friction direction (perpendicular to fdir1). SDF surface/friction/ode/mu2. The primary-direction coefficient is friction/@static. Dimensionless.
attributes.name: mu2

attributes.annotation: Force-dependent slip (compliance) in the first friction direction, in m/s per Newton. SDF surface/friction/ode/slip1. Models tire/track slip. Default: 0 (no slip).
attributes.name: slip1

attributes.annotation: Force-dependent slip (compliance) in the second friction direction, in m/s per Newton. SDF surface/friction/ode/slip2. Default: 0 (no slip).
attributes.name: slip2

named:friction_direction.name: friction_direction

named:frustum.annotation: Frustum (truncated cone/pyramid) for sensor field-of-view visualization. Not a solid physics primitive; use cone/box/cylinder for collision. The shape attribute determines the cross-section: "conical" (circular, uses fov angle) or "pyramidal" (rectangular, uses hfov + vfov). Semantic rule: conical requires fov; pyramidal requires hfov + vfov.

attributes.annotation: Cross-section shape: "conical" (circular, single fov angle) or "pyramidal" (rectangular, hfov + vfov).
attributes.name: shape

named:frustum.name: frustum

named:fuel_cell.annotation: Fuel cell energy source: converts chemical fuel (hydrogen, methanol, etc.) directly to electricity through electrochemical reaction. Unlike batteries (stored charge) or tanks (stored fuel for combustion), fuel cells continuously generate electricity as long as fuel is supplied. The tank element should describe the fuel storage; the fuel cell describes the conversion.
named:fuel_cell.name: fuel_cell

named:geometry.annotation: General geometry container holding exactly one shape. Used for sensor field-of-view geometry (frustum) and general references. NOTE: <visual> uses visual_geometry (primitives only -- a visual mesh is the GLB <model>) and <collision> uses collision_geometry (primitives + lean mesh); both exclude frustum. This type retains mesh + frustum for sensor/FOV usage.
named:geometry.name: geometry

named:gnss_params.annotation: GNSS receiver-specific parameters defining constellation support, correction capabilities, and positioning accuracy. Applies to rf sensors with type="gnss".
named:gnss_params.name: gnss_params

named:gripper_surface.annotation: Gripper or end-effector contact surface that interacts with grasped objects. Describes the physical interface between the robot's gripper and the objects it manipulates. Different gripper types use fundamentally different physics: mechanical fingers squeeze via friction, suction cups use vacuum, magnetic grippers use electromagnetic force, and adhesive surfaces use van der Waals or chemical bonding. An agent uses this to determine grasp feasibility: can this gripper pick up a given object based on weight, material, surface finish, and geometry?

attributes.annotation: Gripper contact mechanism: "mechanical" (friction-based finger pads: the gripper squeezes the object, holding force comes from normal force x friction), "suction" (vacuum cup: single or array of cups creating negative pressure seal, works on smooth non-porous surfaces), "magnetic" (permanent or electromagnetic, works only on ferromagnetic materials), "adhesive" (gecko-inspired dry adhesive or chemical adhesive, uses van der Waals or chemical bonding, works on smooth surfaces regardless of material), "jamming" (granular jamming gripper: conforms to object shape then stiffens via vacuum, handles irregular geometries). Required.
attributes.name: type

named:gripper_surface.name: gripper_surface

named:group_joint_ref.annotation: Reference to a joint within a group.

attributes.annotation: Name of the joint to include in this group.
attributes.name: ref

named:group_joint_ref.name: group_joint_ref

named:group_ref.annotation: Reference to another group (for nested/composite groups).

attributes.annotation: Name of the group to include as a sub-group.
attributes.name: ref

named:group_ref.name: group_ref

named:handedness.annotation: Chirality of a screw thread. right: a right-handed helix (positive @thread_pitch advances along +axis under a right-hand-rule positive rotation), the canonical HCDF storage and the modern gz convention. left: a left-handed helix, the legacy gazebo-classic thread_pitch positive sense. Absent => right (canonical). Only valid on type="screw". Legacy left-handed sources are converted to the canonical right-handed sign on import (a sign flip accompanies the rad_per_m -> m_per_rev unit conversion).
named:handedness.name: handedness

named:hmi_element.annotation: Human-Machine Interface element: displays, speakers, buttons, LEDs, and other devices for human interaction or scene manipulation. Unlike sensors (which observe) and motors (which actuate mechanisms), HMI elements communicate with humans or modify the visual/acoustic environment. Examples: status LEDs on a robot body, a speaker for audio alerts, a touchscreen for operator control, IR illumination LEDs for night-vision cameras, an e-stop button.

attributes.annotation: Unique name for this HMI element within the component.
attributes.name: name

attributes.annotation: HMI element type (display, speaker, buzzer, led-status, led-illumination, button, touchscreen, indicator).
attributes.name: type

attributes.annotation: Name of the visual element containing this HMI's mesh for 3D highlighting.
attributes.name: visual

attributes.annotation: GLTF mesh node name within the visual for 3D highlighting.
attributes.name: mesh

named:hmi_element.name: hmi_element

named:hydrofoil_surface.annotation: Hydrodynamic lifting surface: generates lift in water. Used on underwater vehicles (AUVs), hydrofoil boats, and submarine planes. Same principles as aerofoil but in water (much higher fluid density).
named:hydrofoil_surface.name: hydrofoil_surface

named:include.annotation: Include reference for model composition. Imports another HCDF file's components, joints, and networks into this document. Used to build complex robots from reusable sub-assemblies (e.g., arm module, leg module, sensor head). The included model's components are merged into this document with optional name prefix and pose offset.

attributes.annotation: URI of the HCDF file to include (relative to this document or absolute). Required.
attributes.name: uri

attributes.annotation: SHA-256 hash of the included file for content integrity verification. Optional but recommended for reproducible builds.
attributes.name: sha

attributes.annotation: Name prefix for all elements from the included file. Prevents name collisions when including the same module multiple times (e.g., "left_arm", "right_arm"). Optional.
attributes.name: name

attributes.annotation: Pose offset applied to all included components, as six space-separated doubles "x y z" (meters) then "roll pitch yaw" (radians), relative to the including document's world frame. Optional; default: no offset.
attributes.name: pose

attributes.annotation: If true, the included sub-assembly is imported as a fixed (static) body: its links do not move under dynamics. Maps to SDF include/static. Optional; absent => the included model's own setting.
attributes.name: static

attributes.annotation: Name of a frame within the included model that the @pose is applied to (the frame that gets placed at @pose, rather than the model's default origin). Maps to SDF include/placement_frame. Optional.
attributes.name: placement-frame

named:include.name: include

named:inertial_properties.annotation: Inertial properties of a rigid body component. Defines mass, center of mass, and rotational inertia for dynamics simulation. Equivalent to URDF's inertial element.
named:inertial_properties.name: inertial_properties

named:inertial_sensor.annotation: Inertial measurement sensor (accelerometer, gyroscope, or combined IMU). Contains pose, driver identification, and separate parameter blocks for accelerometer and gyroscope axes.

attributes.annotation: Inertial sensor sub-type. Required. Determines which parameter sub-elements (accel, gyro) are expected.
attributes.name: type

named:inertial_sensor.name: inertial_sensor

named:joint.annotation: Kinematic connection between two components defining degrees of freedom. Supports 10 joint types: revolute (bounded rotation), continuous (unbounded rotation), prismatic (linear), fixed (rigid), ball (3-DOF spherical), universal (2-DOF), planar (2D translation), screw (helical), cylindrical (rotation + translation on same axis), and free (6-DOF unconstrained). Semantic rules: revolute/prismatic/cylindrical require axis + limit; fixed and free forbid axis and limit; universal requires axis + axis2; screw requires axis + thread_pitch; planar requires axis (the plane normal); ball forbids axis/axis2/limit/limit2/thread_pitch (its 3-DOF spherical range is a swing-cone + twist expressed by the ball-only swing_limit/twist_limit elements). Per-DOF limit meaning: cylindrical limit = translation (m), limit2 = rotation (rad, optional); universal limit/limit2 = the two axis limits (rad); planar limit/limit2 = the two in-plane translation ranges (m); screw limit = rotational DOF (rad). Stray-field rules: thread_pitch (and its @pitch_convention/@handedness qualifiers) are only valid on screw; axis2 and dynamics2 are only valid on universal; limit2 is only valid on universal, cylindrical, and planar; swing_limit and twist_limit are only valid on ball.

attributes.annotation: Unique name for this joint (e.g., "left_shoulder_pitch", "wheel_fl_spin"). Required. Referenced by transmission elements and mimic constraints.
attributes.name: name

attributes.annotation: Joint type determining degrees of freedom and required sub-elements. Required.
attributes.name: type

attributes.annotation: Thread pitch for screw joints. Defines the linear advance per full rotation. Canonical HCDF storage is meters-per-revolution, RIGHT-handed (the modern gz screw_thread_pitch convention); legacy gazebo-classic thread_pitch (rad/m, left-handed) is converted to canonical on import (screw_thread_pitch = -2*pi / thread_pitch). attributes.annotation: Upper position limit. Radians for revolute and for a screw <limit> (rotational DOF); meters for prismatic, for a cylindrical <limit> (translation), and for a planar in-plane range. Optional; absence means unbounded. attributes.annotation: Maximum joint effort (torque for revolute in Nm, force for prismatic in N). Default: 0 (unlimited if not specified by tooling).

attributes.annotation: Maximum joint velocity (rad/s for revolute, m/s for prismatic). Default: 0 (unlimited if not specified by tooling).
attributes.name: velocity

attributes.annotation: Maximum joint acceleration (rad/s^2 for revolute, m/s^2 for prismatic). Optional; used for trajectory planning. Maps to the urdfdom v1.2 limit/@acceleration attribute (mirrors urdfdom_headers JointLimits::acceleration); round-trips on HCDF-<->URDF conversion.
attributes.name: acceleration

attributes.annotation: Maximum joint jerk (rad/s^3 for revolute, m/s^3 for prismatic). Optional; used for smooth trajectory generation. Maps to the urdfdom v1.2 limit/@jerk attribute (mirrors urdfdom_headers JointLimits::jerk); round-trips on HCDF-<->URDF conversion.
attributes.name: jerk

attributes.annotation: Maximum joint deceleration (rad/s^2 for revolute, m/s^2 for prismatic). Optional; distinct from acceleration for asymmetric motion profiles. Maps to the urdfdom v1.2 limit/@deceleration attribute (mirrors urdfdom_headers JointLimits::deceleration); round-trips on HCDF-<->URDF conversion.
attributes.name: deceleration

Examples: "home" (standard ready position), "transport" (compact for shipping), "calibration" (known reference for sensor alignment). named:led_illumination.name: led_illumination

named:lidar_params.annotation: Lidar-specific parameters defining scan geometry, point cloud density, and environmental robustness. Applies to optical sensors with type="lidar".
named:lidar_params.name: lidar_params

named:lidar_scan_axis.annotation: One axis of a lidar/ray angular scan pattern, matching a URDF ray <horizontal>/<vertical> element (samples, angular resolution, and min/max sweep angle). This is the lossless target for a converted URDF ray sensor; it complements the aggregate fields (channels, fov) which describe the device rather than the per-axis sampling.

attributes.annotation: Number of samples (beams) along this axis. URDF ray horizontal/vertical @samples.
attributes.name: samples

attributes.name: resolution

attributes.annotation: Minimum sweep angle in radians. URDF ray @min_angle.

attributes.name: max-angle

named:lidar_scan_axis.name: lidar_scan_axis
