named:light_attenuation.name: light_attenuation

named:loop_closure.annotation: Marks a joint as closing a kinematic loop. Contains the predecessor/successor bodies and which DOFs are constrained at the closure point. Used by dynamics solvers (HyRoDyn, Drake) to handle parallel mechanisms that URDF's tree-only structure cannot represent.
named:loop_closure.name: loop_closure

named:measured_value.annotation: A scalar measurement with an optional unit. The text content is the numeric value. HCDF assumes SI units by default: if the unit attribute is omitted, the parent element's documented default SI unit applies (meters for length, kg for mass, radians for angles, seconds for time, Hz for frequency, V for voltage, A for current, W for power, ohm for resistance, Nm for torque, N for force, degC for temperature, Mbps for network speed). Specify unit explicitly only when using a non-SI unit or when the context is ambiguous (e.g., velocity-constant where unit distinguishes Ke from Kv). Example: <speed>100</speed> means 100 Mbps (SI default for speed). <velocity-constant unit="RPM/V">920</velocity-constant> needs explicit unit.

attributes.annotation: Physical unit of the measurement. Optional; if omitted, the SI default for the parent element applies. Specify explicitly for non-SI units (e.g., "RPM/V", "deg", "rpm", "g", "dps", "mK") or when the unit is ambiguous.
attributes.name: unit

named:measured_value.name: measured_value

named:mesh.annotation: External 3D mesh geometry loaded from a file. Supports GLB, glTF, STL, OBJ, and DAE formats.

attributes.annotation: URI of the mesh file (relative to the HCDF document or absolute). Required.
attributes.name: uri

attributes.annotation: Scale factors as three space-separated doubles "sx sy sz" applied to the mesh. Default: "1 1 1" (no scaling).
attributes.name: scale

attributes.annotation: SHA-256 hash of the mesh file for content integrity and content-addressed caching. Optional but recommended for reproducible builds. Mirrors model_ref/@sha so primitive mesh refs are integrity-checkable too.
attributes.name: sha

attributes.annotation: URI of the original pre-conversion asset (e.g. the STL/DAE/OBJ this mesh was converted from when targeting GLB/glTF). Optional; lets tooling reuse the source for a higher-fidelity reverse conversion.
attributes.name: source-uri

named:mesh.name: mesh

named:mimic.annotation: Mimic joint constraint. Makes this joint's position track another joint's position via a linear relationship: position = multiplier * leader_position + offset. Used for mechanically coupled joints (e.g., parallel gripper fingers, coupled four-bar linkages).

attributes.annotation: Name of the leader joint to mimic. Required. Semantic rule: must reference an existing joint defined in the HCDF document.
attributes.name: joint

attributes.annotation: Scaling factor applied to the leader joint's position. Default: 1.0 (identical motion). Use -1 for opposite-direction coupling.
attributes.name: multiplier

attributes.annotation: Constant offset added after scaling (radians for revolute, meters for prismatic). Default: 0.
attributes.name: offset

named:mimic.name: mimic

named:model_ref.annotation: Reference to an external 3D model file (GLB or glTF) for high-fidelity visual representation. Preferred over geometry primitives when available. Optional submesh selectors choose WHICH subtrees of the model this visual draws, in one of three mutually exclusive modes: no selector children draws the WHOLE model (backward compatible; existing docs are unaffected); one or more <submesh> draws the UNION of the named node subtrees (include mode); one or more <exclude-submesh> draws the whole model MINUS the named subtrees (exclude mode). MIXING <submesh> with <exclude-submesh> on one <model> is an ERROR: the modes are exclusive, but the grammar cannot forbid the pair cleanly (both are optional repeated children), so the companion validator rejects the mix rather than the XSD. Selected subtrees KEEP their model-root-relative node transforms (geometry is NOT recentered), so parts split out of one shared GLB keep their authored relative placement. @center on a <submesh> is honored ONLY on a LONE include (a single <submesh>, no siblings, no exclusions) and the validator rejects it on a union member. Two-comps-one-GLB pattern: to split one sha-addressed GLB across two comps joined by a joint, the parent comp includes one subtree and the child comp the complementary subtree of the SAME GLB, and the child visual's <pose> re-expresses that geometry in the child's comp-local frame (the inverse of the joint origin) so the halves still register.

attributes.annotation: URI of the 3D model file (GLB/glTF format). Relative to the HCDF document or absolute. Required.
attributes.name: uri

attributes.annotation: SHA-256 hash of the referenced file for content integrity verification. Optional but recommended for reproducible builds.
attributes.name: sha

named:model_ref.name: model_ref

named:motor.annotation: Motor or actuator with electrical, mechanical, and thermal parameters. Voltage and current use rated_value type with nominal/continuous/peak/max ratings. Connected to joints via transmission elements.

attributes.annotation: Unique name for this motor within the component (e.g., "shoulder_motor", "wheel_fl"). Required. Referenced by transmission elements.
attributes.name: name

attributes.annotation: Motor technology type (bldc, brushed, stepper, servo, linear, hydraulic, pneumatic, thrust, ice). Optional; useful for selecting appropriate control algorithms.
attributes.name: type

attributes.annotation: Motor physical construction: "inrunner" (rotor inside stator, higher RPM, common in industrial servos and drone motors), "outrunner" (rotor outside stator, higher torque, common in hub motors and large drone motors), "axial-flux" (flat pancake design, very thin, high torque density), "pancake" (flat form factor). Only relevant for BLDC/brushed motors.
attributes.name: construction

attributes.annotation: Name of the visual element containing this motor's mesh for 3D highlighting.
attributes.name: visual

attributes.annotation: GLTF mesh node name within the visual for 3D highlighting of this motor.
attributes.name: mesh

attributes.annotation: Name reference to an encoder sensor on this component. Identifies motor-side position feedback. The encoder is a full sensor with its own pose, driver, noise model, and resolution.
attributes.name: encoder

attributes.annotation: Name reference to a Hall sensor on this component used for BLDC commutation. Typically an em-type sensor with 3 Hall elements (U/V/W) providing 6-step commutation signals. Often shares the motor signal connector with the encoder.
attributes.name: hall

attributes.annotation: Name reference to a temperature sensor on this component monitoring motor winding temperature. Typically an NTC thermistor embedded in the motor stator. Used for thermal protection: the agent can monitor temperature and derate or shut down before exceeding max-temperature.
attributes.name: thermistor

named:motor.name: motor

named:noise.annotation: Sensor noise model for simulation. Specifies the statistical distribution and parameters applied to ideal sensor readings. For gaussian type: output = ideal + N(mean, stddev) + bias where bias ~ N(bias-mean, bias-stddev). For uniform type: output = ideal + U(mean - stddev, mean + stddev).

attributes.annotation: Noise distribution type. Required. Use "gaussian" for realistic sensor simulation, "none" for ideal sensors.
attributes.name: type

named:noise.name: noise

named:optical_sensor.annotation: Optical sensor (camera, lidar, ToF, optical flow). Contains one or more field-of-view definitions, each with its own intrinsics, distortion, and noise model.

attributes.annotation: Optical sensor sub-type (camera, thermal, lidar, tof, optical_flow). Required.
attributes.name: type

named:optical_sensor.name: optical_sensor

named:pitch_convention.annotation: Unit convention the screw @thread_pitch value is expressed in. m_per_rev: meters of axial advance per full (2*pi rad) revolution; the canonical HCDF storage and the modern gz screw_thread_pitch convention. rad_per_m: radians of rotation per meter of axial advance; the legacy gazebo-classic thread_pitch convention. Absent => m_per_rev (canonical). Only valid on type="screw". The SDF importer CONVERTS a legacy rad_per_m source to canonical m_per_rev and stores the converted value with this attribute omitted; the attribute exists so a non-canonical pitch can also be authored/preserved explicitly.
named:pitch_convention.name: pitch_convention

named:pose.annotation: 6-DOF pose (position + orientation) of an element relative to its parent frame. Specify position via xyz and orientation via either rpy (Euler angles) or quat (quaternion). If both rpy and quat are given, quat takes precedence.

attributes.annotation: Position as three space-separated doubles "x y z" in meters. Default: "0 0 0" (origin of parent frame).
attributes.name: xyz

attributes.annotation: Orientation as three space-separated Euler angles "roll pitch yaw" in radians (XYZ extrinsic convention). Default: "0 0 0" (no rotation).
attributes.name: rpy

attributes.annotation: Orientation as quaternion "x y z w" (Hamilton convention, scalar-last), exactly four doubles. Optional; if present, overrides rpy (quat-wins precedence).
attributes.name: quat

named:pose.name: pose

attributes.annotation: Unique name for this power source.
attributes.name: name

attributes.annotation: Power source role in the system: "primary" (main power source), "backup" (engaged on primary failure), "hot-swap" (can be replaced while system runs on other source), "ups" (uninterruptible: provides power during switchover). An agent uses this for power redundancy analysis.
attributes.name: role

attributes.annotation: Power source group name for failover pairing. Sources in the same group can substitute for each other. Example: group="main" on two hot-swap batteries means either can power the system alone while the other is replaced.
attributes.name: group

attributes.annotation: Name of the visual element containing this power source's mesh for 3D highlighting.
attributes.name: visual

attributes.annotation: GLTF mesh node name within the visual for 3D highlighting of this power source.
attributes.name: mesh

named:power_source.name: power_source

named:prop_surface.annotation: Propeller surface: generates thrust from rotation. Used on multirotors, fixed-wing aircraft, boats, and underwater vehicles. The associated motor provides torque; the propeller converts it to thrust based on diameter, pitch, and blade geometry.
named:prop_surface.name: prop_surface

named:radar_params.annotation: Radar-specific parameters for 4D imaging radar and distance/velocity sensing. Applies to rf sensors with type="radar".
named:radar_params.name: radar_params

named:radiation_sensor.annotation: Radiation sensor for detecting ionizing radiation. Used on nuclear inspection robots, space robots, and environmental monitoring platforms. Extends sensor_base with radiation type attribute.

attributes.name: type

named:range_value.annotation: A value with minimum and maximum bounds and an optional unit. The text content is the nominal value. attributes.annotation: Physical unit. Optional; SI default applies if omitted.
attributes.name: unit

attributes.annotation: Minimum acceptable value in the specified unit.
attributes.name: min

attributes.annotation: Maximum acceptable value in the specified unit.
attributes.name: max

named:range_value.name: range_value

named:rated_value.annotation: A value with multiple rating levels for motor electrical parameters. Text content is the primary value. attributes.name: name

attributes.annotation: Sensor output update rate in Hz. Applies to all sub-sensors in this group unless overridden. Optional.
attributes.name: update-rate

named:sensor.name: sensor

named:sensor_base.annotation: Base sensor type with elements common to ALL sensor subtypes: pose, driver, range, resolution, noise, data output, and geometry. ODR/bandwidth/FIFO are NOT included here; those are specific to high-rate inertial sensors and live in sensor_params (accel/gyro blocks).
named:sensor_base.name: sensor_base

named:sensor_driver.annotation: Sensor driver identification and configuration. Maps the physical sensor to a software driver by name and provides axis alignment correction for the driver's coordinate frame.

attributes.annotation: Driver identifier string used by the runtime to load the correct sensor driver (e.g., "bmi088", "icm42688p", "bmp390"). Required.
attributes.name: name

named:sensor_driver.name: sensor_driver

named:sensor_fov.annotation: Field-of-view definition for an optical sensor. Each FoV represents a distinct sensing cone/pyramid (e.g., a stereo camera has two FoVs). The intrinsics/distortion elements hold nominal datasheet values; the calibration element holds measured values from an actual calibration on this specific unit. If calibration is present, agents should use it over the design specs.

attributes.annotation: Unique name for this FoV within the sensor (e.g., "left", "right", "depth", "rgb"). Required.
attributes.name: name

attributes.annotation: Visualization color for the FoV cone in the 3D viewer (e.g., "0.2 0.8 0.2 0.3" for translucent green RGBA).
attributes.name: color

named:sensor_fov.name: sensor_fov

named:sensor_params.annotation: Measurement parameters for a sensor axis or channel. Defines the operating range, resolution, sampling rate (ODR), anti-aliasing filter bandwidth, FIFO configuration, and noise model. ODR and bandwidth are distinct: ODR is the hardware sampling rate, bandwidth is the LPF cutoff frequency. The effective processing rate depends on ODR and FIFO watermark.
named:sensor_params.name: sensor_params

named:software.annotation: Firmware or software identity for a component. Used for firmware manifest tracking, version management, and over-the-air update planning.

attributes.annotation: Firmware or software package name (e.g., "zephyr-flight-controller", "linux-jetson-orin"). Required.
attributes.name: name

named:software.name: software

named:solar_source.annotation: Solar panel energy source: converts sunlight to electricity via photovoltaic cells. Used on agricultural robots, exploration rovers, long-endurance UAS, outdoor monitoring platforms, and space systems. Solar provides continuous power during daylight but output varies with irradiance, temperature, panel orientation, and shading. An agent combines solar peak-power with battery capacity to estimate sustained runtime: during daylight the panel charges the battery and powers the system, at night the battery alone provides power.
named:solar_source.name: solar_source

named:sphere.annotation: Sphere geometry primitive centered at the parent pose origin.
named:sphere.name: sphere

attributes.annotation: If true, recenter the selected submesh so its geometric center is at the mesh origin. SDF mesh/submesh/center. Default: false.
attributes.name: center

named:supercapacitor_source.annotation: Supercapacitor (ultracapacitor) energy source: stores energy electrostatically rather than chemically. Compared to batteries: much higher power density (fast charge/discharge in seconds), much lower energy density (stores less total energy), and near-unlimited cycle life (millions of cycles vs hundreds for batteries). Used for peak power buffering (absorbs regenerative braking energy, provides burst current for motor acceleration), bridge power during battery hot-swap, and smoothing pulsed loads. An agent combines supercapacitor burst capability with battery sustained power for complete power budget analysis.
named:supercapacitor_source.name: supercapacitor_source

named:surface.annotation: Inline contact physics for a collision shape: friction, restitution (bounciness), and contact dynamics used by physics simulators. Appears only under <collision>. Not to be confused with <dynamic-surface> (functional aero/wheel/gripper surfaces on a comp).
named:surface.name: surface

This maps 1:1 to Bullet btConeTwistConstraint::setLimit(swing1, swing2, twist), USD UsdPhysicsSphericalJoint (circular/elliptic cone), and MuJoCo's scalar cone (set swing1=swing2, omit twist). Optional; an omitted <swing_limit> means the swing is unbounded (ODE-compatible free ball). Only valid on type="ball".

attributes.annotation: Cone half-angle about local Z, in radians. The maximum swing away from the twist axis in the first perpendicular direction. Required when <swing_limit> is present.
attributes.name: swing1

attributes.annotation: Cone half-angle about local Y, in radians. Omit for a circular cone (defaults to swing1); set different from swing1 for an elliptic cone.
attributes.name: swing2

attributes.annotation: Maximum swing effort (torque, Nm) resisting motion into the cone limit. Default: 0 (unlimited if not specified by tooling).
attributes.name: effort

attributes.annotation: Maximum swing angular velocity (rad/s). Default: 0 (unlimited if not specified by tooling).
attributes.name: velocity

named:tactile_sensor.annotation: Tactile sensor for distributed contact/pressure measurement across a surface. Unlike force sensors (single-point measurement), tactile sensors provide spatially distributed pressure data across an array of sensing elements (taxels). Used on robot fingertips, palms, grippers, and body skin for grasp planning, slip detection, object recognition by touch, and safe physical interaction. Extends sensor_base with tactile-specific parameters: array dimensions, taxel count, spatial resolution, and pressure range.

attributes.annotation: Tactile sensor technology type (capacitive, resistive, piezoelectric, barometric, optical). Required. Determines the sensing principle and typical characteristics: capacitive and barometric are best for static pressure, piezoelectric for dynamic events (slip, texture), optical for rich 3D contact geometry.
attributes.name: type

named:tactile_sensor.name: tactile_sensor

named:tank_source.annotation: Fuel/gas tank energy source. For combustion engines, hydrogen fuel cells, compressed air systems, or pneumatic actuators. Defines fuel type, volume, pressure, energy content, and flow characterization (how fluid exits and at what rate). An agent needs both capacity (how much energy is stored) and flow (how fast it can be delivered) to compute runtime and power capability.
named:tank_source.name: tank_source

named:temperature_sensor.annotation: Temperature sensor: thermistor, RTD, thermocouple, or IR. Common use: motor winding temperature monitoring (NTC thermistor in motor signal connector), ambient temperature, battery cell temperature. Extends sensor_base with temperature sensor type attribute.

attributes.annotation: Temperature sensor type: thermistor (NTC/PTC, common in motors), rtd (PT100/PT1000, high accuracy), thermocouple (K/J/T type, wide range), ir (non-contact infrared). Required.
attributes.name: type

named:temperature_sensor.name: temperature_sensor

named:track_surface.annotation: Tracked vehicle surface (tank treads, rubber tracks). Defines the track geometry and ground contact properties. Used for high-traction vehicles on rough terrain.
named:track_surface.name: track_surface

named:transmission.annotation: Mechanical power transmission connecting motor(s) to joint(s). Defines the gear reduction ratio, efficiency, backlash, and optional compliant elements (springs) for the mechanical coupling between motor output and joint input. A single motor + single joint endpoint is a SIMPLE reduction (the common case). MULTIPLE endpoints express a coupling: a GEARBOX gears two joint endpoints by the reduction ratio (a reference joint and a driven joint, distinguished by the endpoint role attribute); a DIFFERENTIAL couples two motor endpoints to two joint endpoints (role input/output). A transmission without spring elements is a rigid actuator. Adding a series spring creates a Series Elastic Actuator (SEA). Adding a parallel spring creates a Parallel Elastic Actuator (PEA). Both can be combined. Advanced variants (CPEA, AE-PEA, VSA) are expressed through spring attributes (clutch, equilibrium-actuator, stiffness-actuator).

attributes.annotation: Unique name for this transmission (e.g., "shoulder_trans", "wheel_fl_belt"). Required.
attributes.name: name

attributes.annotation: Mechanical transmission type (simple, differential, belt, gear, planetary, cycloidal, harmonic, strain-wave, worm). Optional; defaults to simple if not specified.
attributes.name: type

attributes.annotation: Name reference to a joint-side encoder sensor. This is the encoder on the output side of the transmission (after the gearbox), providing higher-accuracy joint position feedback than the motor-side encoder. Optional: not all transmissions have output encoders.
attributes.name: encoder

attributes.annotation: Name of the visual element containing this transmission's mesh for 3D highlighting.
attributes.name: visual

attributes.annotation: GLTF mesh node name within the visual for 3D highlighting of this transmission.
attributes.name: mesh

named:transmission.name: transmission

named:transmission_endpoint.annotation: Reference to a motor or joint endpoint in a transmission. Uses a slash-path "comp/motor" (or "comp/joint") to identify the target across components: the last '/'-separated segment is the leaf (the motor or joint name), everything before it names the component, and a bare leaf name is legal iff it is document-unique. Slash is the ONLY reference separator: a dot is not a separator. In a multi-endpoint coupling (gearbox, differential) the optional role attribute disambiguates this endpoint's part in the coupling. Endpoint resolution is deferred to the companion validator.

attributes.annotation: Slash-path reference to the motor or joint (e.g., "shoulder_comp/shoulder_motor", or the bare "shoulder_joint" when it is document-unique). The last '/'-separated segment is the leaf (motor or joint name); everything before it names the component; leaf names contain no separator. Slash is the only accepted separator: a dot is not a reference separator. Required.
attributes.name: ref

attributes.annotation: Optional role of this endpoint within a multi-endpoint coupling: reference/driven for a gearbox (which joint is the geared reference and which is driven), input/output for a differential (which motors are inputs and which joints are outputs). Omit for a simple single-motor/single-joint reduction, where the endpoint's role is unambiguous.
attributes.name: role

named:transmission_endpoint.name: transmission_endpoint

named:transmission_spring.annotation: Compliant element (spring) in a transmission drivetrain. The presence of a spring element is what distinguishes compliant actuators from rigid ones. A spring in series between the gearbox and the joint output creates a Series Elastic Actuator (SEA): enabling torque sensing via deflection measurement, impact absorption, backdrivability through high-ratio gearboxes, and inherent safety for human interaction. A spring in parallel with the motor creates a Parallel Elastic Actuator (PEA): providing passive gravity compensation to reduce motor effort. Multiple spring elements are allowed: an SEA+PEA combination uses one series spring for force sensing and one parallel spring for gravity compensation. Advanced variants add a clutch (CPEA, clutchable PEA, engages/disengages the parallel spring on demand), an equilibrium motor (AE-PEA, adjustable equilibrium PEA, shifts the spring rest position at runtime), or a stiffness motor (VSA, variable stiffness actuator, changes spring stiffness at runtime via a second motor).

attributes.annotation: Where the spring sits in the drivetrain relative to the gearbox and motor. "series": between gearbox output and joint output (SEA): the spring deflects under load, enabling force sensing via dual-encoder deflection measurement and providing inherent compliance. "parallel": alongside the motor, between a fixed anchor and the joint output (PEA): the spring provides a passive torque that assists or opposes the motor, typically tuned for gravity compensation. Required.
attributes.name: placement

attributes.annotation: Physical spring construction: "torsion-bar" (solid or tubular bar that twists, compact, common in SEAs), "leaf" (flat spring that bends, easy to manufacture), "coil" (helical compression/extension spring, common in linear actuators), "cable-linear" (cable-driven with linear spring in tension), "gas" (gas spring, provides near-constant force over stroke), "custom" (application-specific design). Optional.
attributes.name: type

attributes.annotation: How joint torque is measured using this spring. "spring-deflection": torque derived from the angular difference between motor-side and output-side encoders multiplied by spring stiffness (torque = k x delta_theta): the standard SEA approach, requires two encoders. "strain-gauge": dedicated strain gauge or load cell on the spring element (e.g., Franka Panda joint torque sensors). "current": torque estimated from motor current (torque = Kt x I): less accurate, no spring needed but listed here for completeness. "none": no torque sensing. Optional; only applicable for series springs.
attributes.name: torque-sensing

attributes.annotation: Clutch mechanism for engaging/disengaging a parallel spring (CPEA). "electromagnetic": fast switching (2-10 ms), requires continuous power to hold engaged. "mechanical-latch": zero holding power, slower switching (10-50 ms), uses a bistable mechanism. "one-way": ratchet or sprag clutch that locks in one direction and freewheels in the other. "none" or omit: no clutch, spring is permanently engaged. Only applicable for parallel springs.
attributes.name: clutch

attributes.annotation: Reference to a motor (slash-path "comp/motor", or a bare motor name when document-unique) that adjusts the spring equilibrium position for AE-PEA configurations. This second motor is typically small and slow: it only moves when the operating posture changes, shifting where the parallel spring exerts zero force for optimal gravity compensation at any joint angle. Only applicable for parallel springs with equilibrium-range.
attributes.name: equilibrium-actuator

attributes.annotation: Reference to a motor (slash-path "comp/motor", or a bare motor name when document-unique) that adjusts spring stiffness at runtime for Variable Stiffness Actuator (VSA) configurations. The second motor changes the effective lever arm or preload on the spring, varying stiffness between the min and max values specified in the stiffness element. Only applicable for series springs with variable stiffness range.
attributes.name: stiffness-actuator

named:visual.annotation: Visual representation of a component for rendering. Contains either a high-fidelity 3D model reference or a geometry primitive fallback (or both, where model is preferred and geometry is the fallback). Multiple visuals per component are allowed for multi-part rendering.

attributes.annotation: Unique name for this visual within the component. Required. Used for programmatic toggling and identification.
attributes.name: name

attributes.annotation: Toggle group name. Visuals sharing the same toggle group can be shown/hidden together at runtime (e.g., "leds", "covers").
attributes.name: toggle

attributes.annotation: Provenance of the name (authored vs converter-synthesized). Optional; absence means authored. A converter importing URDF (whose visuals have no name) sets this to "synthesized" so the name can be stripped on URDF export.
attributes.name: name-origin

named:visual.name: visual

named:visual_geometry.annotation: Visual geometry: primitive shapes ONLY (box, cylinder, sphere, capsule, cone, ellipsoid). There is deliberately NO <mesh> here -- a *visual* mesh is the self-contained GLB/glTF <model> (the rich-appearance arm of <visual>), never a bare geometry mesh. So "a visual mesh is GLB-only" is enforced by the grammar itself. Frustum is excluded (sensor-FOV only). Used in <visual>'s flat/primitive arm with an optional flat <color>.
named:visual_geometry.name: visual_geometry

named:wheel_surface.annotation: Wheel ground contact surface. Defines the tire/wheel geometry and friction properties for ground vehicles. The motor driving this wheel is defined separately; the wheel surface describes the contact interface with the ground.

attributes.annotation: Wheel type: "driven" (has motor), "steering" (steerable), "caster" (passive swivel), "omni" (omnidirectional rollers), "mecanum" (45-degree rollers). Optional.
attributes.name: type
